review_text: Không khí tuyệt vời với thức ăn tuyệt vời. Chúng tôi gọi hai món và họ phục vụ rất nhanh. Cụ thể hơn, chúng tôi đã gọi món Bún Bò Huế và Cơm Chiên Cá Mặn. Cả hai đều tuyệt vời. Nhân viên rất chu đáo; nói chung là một trải nghiệm rất thú vị.

address: 42 Võ Văn Kiệt, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Nếu bạn đang tìm kiếm địa điểm tuyệt vời để thư giãn ở trung tâm Quận 1 thì đây là địa điểm không thể bỏ qua. Nó tạo ra sự cân bằng hoàn hảo, sôi động, nơi du khách quốc tế và người dân địa phương hiểu biết tụ tập, tạo ra một bầu không khí vừa náo nhiệt vừa chào đón. Ngoài những rung cảm tuyệt vời, thực đơn còn là một bức thư tình dành cho ẩm thực Việt Nam chính thống. Cho dù bạn là người mới đến hay là người địa phương dày dặn kinh nghiệm, cam kết của họ đối với hương vị truyền thống khiến nơi đây trở thành lựa chọn nổi bật cho những ai muốn thưởng thức hương vị Sài Gòn đích thực ngay tại trung tâm thành phố.

review_text: Tôi đã có trải nghiệm tuyệt vời tại nhà hàng này! Đã đến đó 2 lần. Đồ ăn rất ngon và dịch vụ thì tuyệt vời! review_text: Nhà hàng trống rỗng khi chúng tôi đến nhưng có thêm 3 bàn nữa khi chúng tôi ngồi trên lầu. Chỉ có 3 bàn lớn hơn và một quầy trên tầng chính. Khoảng 8 bàn trên tầng 2 có nhà vệ sinh. review_text: If you're looking for an authentic Western-style lunch spot near Bau Cat Market, this is the number one choice. I frequently visit this restaurant for lunch and absolutely love their sour fish soup. The fish here is fresh and fatty, and the broth is rich and flavorful, truly authentic to the Western region: tangy, subtly sweet, and fragrant with sawtooth coriander and Vietnamese coriander. Every time I come, I order this dish because it's so delicious with rice. The restaurant has a casual, clean atmosphere and quick service, making it perfect for office workers or market-goers. The prices are also very reasonable and affordable considering the quality of the food. It's right opposite Bau Cat Market, so it's easy to find. I'll definitely be coming back to enjoy their "legendary" sour fish soup!

The rice is soft and fragrant, and the food is warmed up by microwave when customers arrive, making it very appetizing. The bitter melon soup, sour fish soup with catfish, and snakehead fish soup are rich and flavorful. The owner is cheerful and friendly. review_text: My hometown restaurant is one of my favorite places to eat when I'm looking for a quiet, simple yet high-quality dining experience. The restaurant has a small but cozy space with a well-designed layout, giving me the feeling of eating at home. The dishes here are prepared quite simply but are very delicious and flavorful. I often choose dishes like chicken stir-fried with lemongrass and chili, sour fish soup, stir-fried water spinach with garlic, and braised pork with eggs. All the food is served hot and fragrant. The prices are quite reasonable, suitable for all budgets. The staff are very attentive and friendly, always ready to answer any questions or requests from customers. However, the only drawback is the slightly cramped space, which might make dining a bit difficult for large groups. However, this is only a minor drawback and doesn't affect the quality or my trust in my hometown restaurant. In summary, Com Que Toi is a great choice for those seeking a quiet and cozy space to enjoy delicious, flavorful dishes.

review_text: A no-frills, satisfying bowl of pho — clean beef broth, tender slices of beef, and generous herbs and onions on top. Nothing fancy about the setting, but that's part of the charm; it felt like a proper neighborhood spot rather than a tourist stop. Good portion size and fair prices. address: 241 - 243 Nguyễn Trãi, Cầu Ông Lãnh, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: First of all, foreigner coming here for the first time, be ready for ONLY CASH. Casual atmosphere, no western level service, but the waiter and the waitress are very helpful. Food is very quickly served, no time for looking at the Google reviews while you wait. I ordered a Pho Special with all sorts of meat on top of the noodles. Very tasty. I will memorize this as my Pho benchmark. No AC, but the fans are enough to keep you comfortable even in the hottest month of April. So, definitely worth a visit. Try coming on a Grab Bike, the ride will warm up yourself for a nice cosy Vietnamese experience.

address: 241 - 243 Nguyễn Trãi, Cầu Ông Lãnh, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam

address: 241 - 243 Nguyễn Trãi, Cầu Ông Lãnh, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5 — Authentic pho, Michelin-recognised for a reason Visited Phở Hùng near Ben Thanh Market in Ho Chi Minh City, and it absolutely lived up to its Michelin Guide recognition (2024–2025). This is a no-frills, very local spot serving excellent, authentic pho at very reasonable prices. The atmosphere feels genuinely Vietnamese — simple, bustling, and focused on the food. I tried the house special pho, and it was outstanding. The broth was deep, aromatic, and clean, with generous portions of beef and well-balanced flavours. Add in the fresh herbs, bean sprouts, and chilli to taste, and it’s comfort food at its best. To top it off, they also serve traditional Vietnamese iced coffee, which was strong, smooth, and the perfect finish to the meal. If you’re looking for a true local pho experience in Ho Chi Minh City — especially one backed by Michelin — Phở Hùng is absolutely worth a visit.

address: 241 - 243 Nguyễn Trãi, Cầu Ông Lãnh, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: If you ever come to Ho Chi Minh City, I really hope you give this beef noodle shop a chance. It’s located in District 1, so it’s very convenient to visit. The pricing is reasonable and the portions are generous. The soup base is clear yet flavorful, with a light sweetness and a very comforting aroma. The noodles are smooth with a slightly rough texture, which gives them a nice chewy bite. One great bonus is that the side vegetables are free-flow, so you can add as much as you like. I highly recommend the fat beef brisket. Don’t worry about the word “fat” — it’s definitely worth trying. The meat is soft and chewy, and surprisingly not oily or greasy at all. Overall, it’s a satisfying and hearty bowl of beef noodles. If you’re in District 1, why not give it a try? 👍

address: 14 Phạm Hồng Thái, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Arrived here on a weekday lunchtime, heard its a Michelin Guide restaurant so was a little worried it might be crowded. When I arrived, I saw the shop and wanted to enter, then the staff told me to go to the other store. I was wondering if he was driving me away, but then he told me they have a bigger shop same name a few units down. I walked a few meters and reached the bigger shop, and when I walked in was immediately given a table and menu. Decided to get a kamquat juice and a stone bowl mixed pho. The experience was quite interesting because I was immediately served a basket of greens and water cooked beansprouts, and then a plate of noodles and raw beef. Am quite surprised that the noodles looked different but am excited to try their home made noodles. Also am impressed they keep the thin slices of raw beef uncooked so we could cook by ourselves according to the preference we want for how well the meat should be cooked. Ordered an egg also so I could pour into the pho soup later. The stone bowl came with a lot of beef balls cut into smaller bite size pieces. I started pouring the noodles and beef slices in and i could take the slices out as soon as they were medium rare by not leaving it in the soup for too long. Basically this is a bowl of flawless pho, very impressed with the quality for such a simple dish. The noodles texture was so soft and smooth and the beef you can tailor to the level you like it so it's just a win win for all. So simple yet so impressive. The kamquat juice is also a must try as it was really so cooling and refreshing on a hot and humid Ho Chi Minh weather. This is definitely the one place I would recommend for the pho lovers to visit and it definitely lives up to its name.

address: 14 Phạm Hồng Thái, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: PHỞ VIỆT NAM Review (late post but worth it) This is a very late review (like 3 months late 😅), but this spot definitely deserves it. If you’re looking for a proper local meal, this place delivers. We ordered the Wagyu beef pho served in a hot stone bowl, and the soup stayed hot the entire time, no sad, lukewarm broth halfway through. Solid experience from start to finish. Service was quick and efficient. Even without a reservation, we were seated right on time, which honestly feels rare these days. Definitely lives up to being a Michelin-recommended spot. Good food, smooth service, no unnecessary fuss. Highly recommended if you want legit pho without the guesswork.

address: 14 Phạm Hồng Thái, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: I got the stone bowl pho with the wagyu beef and it was so good. Also got a passion fruit juice as well. Would recommend!

address: 14 Phạm Hồng Thái, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Phở Việt Nam was a great spot for a proper local meal and definitely lived up to expectations! We ordered the bắp hoa and phở tái đá, and both dishes were packed with flavour. The broth was rich and aromatic, and the meat was very fresh and tender. Portions were generous, so you’re definitely getting good value for what you pay. The staff were friendly and welcoming, and one of them spoke good English which made ordering easy. He recommended the dishes we got, and they turned out to be great choices. There were heaps of sides to customise your meal, along with a large selection of sauces so you can adjust everything to your taste. It made the whole experience feel a bit more interactive and authentic. The location is convenient and easy to find, and everything felt clean and well run. Overall, a really enjoyable experience with great food, good service, and solid value. Would definitely come back again.

address: 14 Phạm Hồng Thái, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Really good pho, very reasonable pricing in prime tourist area, definitely a must visit. I love eating outdoors on the small red stool, it gives off a very friendly family owned vibe. The service was excellent, we had a very friendly lady take our order and dropped off ice tea for us. The food came out quickly and it was delicious. I love that they make the pho noodle in house so it was definitely unique in terms of taste and texture. The broth was flavorful without being fatty/ oily and gave off a very clean taste. All the meat we had in the pho was very tender, the oxtail was most surprising since it came off the bone very easily. Definitely worthy of Michelin guide for the last 3 years 🙂

address: 25 Mạc Đĩnh Chi, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: The pho here is decent. It’s cooked in a traditional style because I can tell the broth is simmered from bones without many added spices like star anise or cinnamon (there might be some, but so little that I can’t really taste them). The broth is light, clear, and not as rich or heavily seasoned as in other places. I heard from locals that the owner is from Northern Vietnam, but the flavor tastes more like Southern-style pho. The noodles are thin rather than the long, flat noodles typical of Northern pho. The restaurant is quite small but very clean—a family-run place. The price is a bit high, and the portion of meat isn’t large, but the quality is good. The beef isn’t mushy; it’s firm and slightly chewy. The beef balls here are very delicious (I’d say it’s one of the places with the best beef balls, in my opinion). The photo below shows a bowl of pho priced at 90,000 VND. It’s worth trying at least once when you’re here. It’s just a bit of a pity that they don’t serve fried dough sticks.

address: 64 Trần Khánh Dư, Tân Định, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: phở hải at 64 trần khánh dư is that spot that just gets it right the late night savior they're open late, making this the ultimate move for when that pho craving hits after dark. no more sad midnight snacks when you can get the real deal. the broth situation we're talking about a clear, deeply savory broth that's been simmered for hours - it's rich without being heavy. keeping it real though, the broth leans a bit sweet for my taste, but the depth of flavor still hits different. the protein perfection they absolutely nail the texture game with their beef - whether you go with rare steak that melts in your mouth or the brisket that's fall-apart tender, every cut is consistently on point. the meat-to-noodle ratio is always fire. the tân định vibes tucked away in this historic neighborhood, the place has major local gem energy. no fancy decor, just focused pho craftsmanship and the comforting sounds of bowls being enjoyed. it's the real deal without trying too hard. the final call if you don't mind a slightly sweeter broth and want that perfect late-night pho fix without the tourist crowds, this place absolutely delivers. don't forget to ❤️.

address: 64 Trần Khánh Dư, Tân Định, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: My noodle quest took an unexpected detour today! I accidentally adventured into the wrong shop this morning. The real treasure is tucked inside a little lane, basically playing diagonal peek-a-boo with the famous "Crab Noodle 87". Think of my first stop as the polite, "proper" cousin. This place? It's the spicy, rebellious sibling with their condiments. The vibe here is turned up to 11—literally! It's like a delicious sauna in the best way. And the condiments? Game-changer. Their blended red chili padi is a fiery little cloud of joy. Verdict: Absolutely worth the hunt! Just be ready for two quirks: the tables are practically knee-high (think charmingly awkward picnic), and they swap in thinner vermicelli noodles instead of the wider type, Kway teow. A smol table and slim noodles are a tiny price to pay for chili heaven! 10/10 would get happily lost again. A beef noodle seller from Singapore.

address: 64 Trần Khánh Dư, Tân Định, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: It's Phở restaurant. All tables are on the street beside the shop. It can say that it's street food. Anyway there was one guy who speak English, so I could order smoothly. Then I had a bowl of Phở with brisket. It's south style Pho, then soup is a bit sweet. The meat was tender and enough amount for the price. It was great Pho, even comparing the one selected by Michelin. But it's better to have lid or cover for the lemon and hearbs because everything are on the tables outside.

address: 34-36 Trần Hưng Đạo, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Very attractive looking restaurant from outside, with signs indicating it was tourist friendly, and would offer visitors to Saigon, the authentic Pho experience. Inside were roomy tables with great decor and artwork presenting a very welcoming and comfortable, air conditioned eating place. Outside, and more streetfood type appearance, with an impressive curved corner display and more outside tables. The menu is aimed at the visiting tourists, with dishes, that visitors might recognise, and also would certainly satisfy the hungry revellers from the nearby Bui Vien. Although we did consider the prices here a little high, this is a major tourist area, and is to be expected. The meals served were tasty and well presented. They were quickly prepared and the staff were keen and attentive.

address: 34-36 Trần Hưng Đạo, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: While in Ho Chi Minh City, Pho Phat Tai became our go-to spot and a place we kept going back to. The pho we had was so good, and honestly, some of the best we had while we were there. Big shoutout to Nguyen as well, such a legend. He was always welcoming and made the place feel really friendly and easy to come back to. Would definitely recommend Pho Phat Tai if you’re in Ho Chi Minh.

address: 34-36 Trần Hưng Đạo, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Very nice place to eat authentic Vietnamese pho!! All the staff is very kind and helpful for all your needs. The price is good and for the quality you eat. A top experience for a beatiful dinner in an amazing place! A must go in ho chi minh city.

address: 34-36 Trần Hưng Đạo, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: 내돈내산 I visited at lunchtime when the weather was very hot. Even though there were many customers inside the restaurant didn’t turn on the air conditioning or any fans. There was only one fan near the cashier and it was only pointed toward me after I mentioned how hot it was. That already felt uncomfortable and inattentive. I ordered a glass of orange juice but after waiting for a while the staff brought it in from outside. It felt like they had gone out to buy it and then sold it to customers. I honestly found this hard to understand. Coming back to Vietnam and not being able to drink a proper glass of orange juice was very disappointing. The drink was basically just ice, sugar, and half an orange. My disappointment started with the beverage. The food itself came out quite quickly but the first impression of the pho broth was a strong unpleasant smell, like bones that hadn’t been properly prepared. The meat and rice noodles were fine, but the bowl was still just average, similar to many other pho places. I actually came all the way from District 2 because of google reviews so realizing the experience didn’t live up to expectations made it feel even more like a waste of time and effort. The final downside was that the restaurant didn’t even provide paper napkins. I had to use wet tissues I brought with me. This visit felt like wasted time, wasted money, and a real disappointment. Maybe something went wrong that day, but based on my lunchtime experience, I was not satisfied at all.

address: 34-36 Trần Hưng Đạo, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: The best restaurant in the city! High-quality food, absolutely delicious dishes, very fast service, and reasonable prices 👌🏼 Highly recommended if you’re looking for a great dining experience!

address: 413 - 415 Nguyễn Trãi, An Đông, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: My dad has been coming here for 30+ years and he always brings me here for daddy daughter dates so this place holds a very special place in my heart. Objectively speaking, the pho broth is incredibly clean yet flavorful. I’m not quenching for thirst after I eat here so I don’t think they add as much msg. The sweetness of the broth really comes from all the beef bones and different cuts of beef. Noodles are fresh and delicious, typical for Vietnam but I live in the states so it’s impressive for me. The beef is a bit on the tougher side but that’s just Vietnamese beef. They’re not getting massages or listening to jazz music. Overall I’d choose this over some fancy wagyu pho. Even the hoisin sauce is delicious.

address: 413 - 415 Nguyễn Trãi, An Đông, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: I came all the way to District 5 to check out this famous Pho spot. I ordered the mixed beef Pho, and the broth was definitely the highlight—it was incredibly clear, sweet, and flavorful. However, I found the beef to be a bit overcooked for my personal preference. Next time, I would definitely go for the rare beef (Pho Tai) version to get that tender texture. While the food was good overall, I traveled here from District 1, and to be honest, I probably wouldn’t make the long trip specifically just to eat here again. But if you are already in the area, it is certainly a solid choice for a bowl of authentic Pho. Great taste, but maybe not worth a special cross-district journey if you're staying far away.

address: 413 - 415 Nguyễn Trãi, An Đông, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: The pho here was honestly amazing 🍲✨ The broth was rich, flavorful, and tasted so fresh. Portions were very generous with a lot of meat, and everything was served perfectly. We randomly found this place while walking around District 5 and were really impressed. Cozy atmosphere, delicious food, and definitely a spot we’ll come back to again 🤍

address: 413 - 415 Nguyễn Trãi, An Đông, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Don’t expect street food prices here but portion is set more as well. Short walk from our hotel in District 5. They knew we were tourists so advised us to go upstairs for the air conditioning. Yes, the beef is chopped up which I think makes Kaju Tofu more tender. Son ordered just the beef and we had the dac biet (combo with everything) Food was good only slight was the workers looked miserable. But I guess you really don’t go out to eat in Vietnam for the smiles.

address: 413 - 415 Nguyễn Trãi, An Đông, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Pho le was in a bunch of recommended lists, so we opted to try it as well. Verdict: it was mid, not as flavorful as i thought, nothing stood out. It wasnt bad, very big portions and good pricing. Might opt for pho somewhere else next time. Lots of seating, multiple floors. Cash only btw.

address: 260C Pasteur, Phường, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Came here around 8 PM and the restaurant was still open, which was perfect for a late dinner. I ordered the mixed beef pho, along with Vietnamese pork sausage, fresh shrimp spring rolls, and youtiao (fried dough sticks). The fresh herbs and vegetables, as well as the fried dough sticks, are placed on the table for you to enjoy with your pho. I added plenty of onions, spring onions, and cilantro — just the way I like it. 🌿 The pho tasted really good and the broth was flavorful. One thing to note is that they don’t serve the pho in a hot pot like Pho VietNam does, so the soup isn’t kept boiling hot throughout the meal. But honestly, it was still delicious and satisfying. Another plus: they accept credit cards, which is always convenient when traveling. Overall, a really good spot for a simple, comforting bowl of Vietnamese pho, especially if you’re looking for a late-night meal. 🍜

address: 260C Pasteur, Phường, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: This was hands down the best pho I had in Saigon for me. The chilli on the table added a lot to it as I am a spice lover so having some bit of normal tasty pho soup and mixing it up with spoonfuls of chilli for a spiced pho take with either beef (which was what I had no.1 raw beef) or beef balls was just so good. Drink wise the ice blended Caramel Machiato Coffee was the usual nice and sweet. The fresh and fried spring rolls are both good and the overall meal was excellent.

address: 260C Pasteur, Phường, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Must-visit legendary Pho spot in Saigon! 🍜 A short walk from the iconic Pink Church (Tân Định Church). The beef quality is excellent, and the broth is flavorful, rich, and perfectly balanced. The portions are quite generous—I’m a light eater, so I couldn't even finish my bowl! 😅 Also, don't miss their fresh sugarcane juice—perfectly sweet and super refreshing after walking around in the heat. Highly recommended! 😋

address: 260C Pasteur, Phường, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Great late lunch at Pho Hoa Pasteur. This is a very well organized clean and delicious dining choice! Restaurant was busy although seated immediately and food served rapidly. Dined on the Pho Tia and Banh Pate. A generous setup of veggies sprouts lime and chili accompanied the Pho the broth was complex and incredibly delicious filled with tender beef. Wonderfully tasty Banh Pateso filled to the brim with pate! Looking forward to my next visit!

address: 260C Pasteur, Phường, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Solid food! tastes like home even though I’m not from Vietnam. I will definitely come back! The serving size is generous and the ingredients are not skimped on. Really great value for money. Overall, it’s a “bang for your buck” experience. Highly recommended!

address: 8 Đ. Kỳ Đồng, Nhiêu Lộc, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: I think the Pho is just okay not as good as other popular Pho restaurants I have been to. However, I really like their beef balls. They serve a whole beef ball not sliced up and thin. You can have instant noodle instead of pho noddle if you want. I like how they give you a lot of greens.

address: 8 Đ. Kỳ Đồng, Nhiêu Lộc, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Delicious Pho. I had the beef Pho and I really enjoyed it, meat was good and broth was flavorful. Restaurant war spotless clean. Service was pretty good and friendly. Price is also pretty competitive, it is posted on the walls so no worries of getting overcharged. There is no menu but you can point to the wall what meat you want.

address: 8 Đ. Kỳ Đồng, Nhiêu Lộc, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: When I arrive at Pho Anh they specialize in pho and the broth is so beefy and taste amazing. Currently 2025 the quality of the food is amazing full staff and the aroma of pho is just screams goodness I recommend this to family and friends all day. Love the Pug mascot

address: 8 Đ. Kỳ Đồng, Nhiêu Lộc, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: This place is my childhood Pho. It's hard to explain how amazing their Pho taste. I missed this place for 20 years. Finally i got chance to visit Vietnam. I wish i live closer, i would eat this dish everyday.

address: 8 Đ. Kỳ Đồng, Nhiêu Lộc, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Pho is good in this place. Soup is so taste, beef is so soft and delicious. In my point of view, price 45k/1 is so higher than normal. This place has so many staff, it is not suitable with quite narrow place. Thus, it is the good place recommended for you and your family.

address: 63/6 Pasteur, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Phở Minh – Pasteur Located in a small alley on Pasteur Street in the heart of District 1, Phở Minh is a familiar spot for many pho lovers. Despite not being on the main street, the restaurant is always busy thanks to its traditional flavors and has been recognized by the Michelin Guide in the Bib Gourmand category. The broth is clear and rich, with fresh beef options such as rare, brisket, and fatty cuts, delivering an authentic Vietnamese pho experience. The space is simple and cozy, creating the feeling of enjoying a traditional family-style bowl of pho in the heart of Saigon. The clientele is diverse, ranging from locals to international tourists. If you love Vietnamese cuisine in general and pho in particular, this is definitely a place worth trying. Best for: Traditional pho lovers, travelers looking to explore Vietnamese cuisine, and anyone wanting to enjoy a quality bowl of pho right in the center of Ho Chi Minh City.

address: 63/6 Pasteur, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: I recently visited this pho restaurant and had a fairly good experience overall. While the pho was decent, I personally did not find the broth as rich or flavorful as I expected. The taste was acceptable and enjoyable enough, but it lacked the deep and bold flavor that makes a bowl of pho truly memorable. However, one thing I really appreciated was the quality and freshness of the toppings. The meat was fresh, tender, and served in generous portions. The additional ingredients were also well-prepared, which helped make the meal more enjoyable. Another positive point is that everything on the table was kept very clean and organized. The chopsticks, spoons, fresh herbs, lime, and chili were arranged neatly and looked hygienic, which made the dining experience feel more comfortable and professional. The restaurant does not have air conditioning, so it can feel quite hot during the hot summer weather in Saigon, especially around 8-10 AM. This may be something to consider if you prefer cooler dining spaces. In terms of pricing, the restaurant is slightly more expensive compared to some other pho places. I ordered two regular bowls of pho, two iced teas, two pâté chaud pastries, and one extra portion of meat, and the total came to 275,000 VND. Even though the prices are on the higher side, it is still understandable because the restaurant is located in District 1, right in the center of the city. One of the best parts of the experience was definitely the staff. They were very friendly, enthusiastic, and welcoming throughout the meal. Their warm and attentive service created a pleasant atmosphere and left a positive impression. Overall, while the pho itself may not be the most outstanding in terms of flavor, the fresh ingredients, clean setup, central location, and especially the kind staff still make this restaurant a decent place to visit.

address: 63/6 Pasteur, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Warning: Cash only! We came here for breakfast without any cash 🤣 and had to walk around looking for a money exchange place. Luckily, there was one right next to the ice cream shop nearby. We ordered one medium bowl of pho with all the meats to share, plus an extra side of tendon. The pho was decent — good, but not particularly memorable. This place is listed in the Michelin Guide, so I guess the flavor is designed to be balanced and approachable for most people. Nothing too strong or overwhelming. They open only until 10.30am so make sure to come before they close. Overall, it’s worth trying at least once, especially if you want to check out a well-known spot, but personally I wouldn’t say it was anything extraordinary.

address: 63/6 Pasteur, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Stopped by at 10:30 on a Sunday and thought I had missed my chance—the shop was basically sold out and getting ready to close. But when they saw a tired tourist walk in, they kindly made an exception and still served me. That kind of hospitality is something you don’t forget. Cash only! 🤣The pho was comforting, light, and soothing, perfect for a slow morning. The portion was on the smaller side, but the restaurant was spotless and the staff were incredibly polite throughout my visit. If you want the full selection, come early—this place is popular for a reason and sells out fast. Highly recommended for authentic pho and genuine Vietnamese hospitality.

address: 63/6 Pasteur, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Tucked down a little alleyway in the main part of D1, this is a pho establishment that’s been run by the same family for over 80 years. Pho broth is clean and light, meat toppings are well cooked and generous. Pa te so is nice and light, but delicious. Staff are extremely friendly, they held our baby as we ate! Lovely place, would definitely come back.

address: 435 Lý Thái Tổ, Vườn Lài, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: It's Pho restaurant. This is the oldest Pho restaurant in Vietnam. They open only in the morning, I think. When I came afternoon, it was closed. There are two shops with same name, I tried right hand side shop with the staffs with red shirt. The Pho was really nice, mistakenly I had large bowl, and it was really large.

address: 435 Lý Thái Tổ, Vườn Lài, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: If you’d like to experience Phở the Southern Vietnamese way, you’re in for a treat. While this Tàu Bay Phở originally comes from Nam Định Province and has a history spanning more than 70 years, people in Southern Vietnam have embraced it with their own distinctive touch. A bowl of Southern-style phở is often served with a generous plate of fresh herbs such as basil, culantro, and spring onions. These aromatic greens blend beautifully with the rich broth, creating the unforgettable flavor that makes Vietnamese phở famous around the world. Another wonderful thing about phở is that you can choose your favorite cut of beef. My personal recommendation is “Vè” beef—a unique cut that offers the perfect balance of tender meat and slightly crunchy, gelatinous fat. The contrast in texture makes every bite incredibly satisfying. Simple, fragrant, and comforting. This is phở at its finest, enjoyed the Southern Vietnamese way.

address: 435 Lý Thái Tổ, Vườn Lài, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Got recommended by the concierge at the hotel. It is a mom and pop shop the soup has msg but alot a shit tonne of beef bones meats so there is a beef flavour there. Ordered a large mixed bowl with a side of the beef oil in scallions. Overall the pho was decent and for 90k a large okay pricing .

address: 435 Lý Thái Tổ, Vườn Lài, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Don’t eat here, the pho (specifically broth) is very bland and they do not offer bean sprouts. The meat is not delicious, it’s tough. And I’ll say it again, the broth is tasteless. No flavour at all!

address: 435 Lý Thái Tổ, Vườn Lài, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Pho Tàu Bay: A Timeless Classic Since 1954 Pho Tàu Bay is more than just a restaurant; it’s a living testament to the enduring appeal of authentic Vietnamese cuisine. Established in 1954, this venerable institution has become a cornerstone for lovers of pho and traditional Vietnamese dishes. Its history alone lends the establishment an air of authenticity and reverence, but it’s the quality of the food that keeps people coming back. Food: The pho here is a standout, with a rich, flavorful broth that embodies the art of slow simmering. Whether you choose rare beef, brisket, or tendon, the ingredients are always fresh and perfectly balanced. Accompanying herbs, lime, and bean sprouts are crisp and generous, letting you tailor your bowl to perfection. Beyond pho, the menu offers a variety of classic Vietnamese staples such as Bún Bò Huế, Gỏi Cuốn (spring rolls), and Cơm Tấm (broken rice). Each dish feels like a lovingly crafted recipe passed down through generations. Ambiance: Pho Tàu Bay embraces a simple, no-frills environment, which allows the focus to remain firmly on the food. The retro decor and modest furnishings echo its long history, creating a nostalgic atmosphere that transports you to an earlier time. It’s not about fancy presentation but about honest, soul-satisfying meals. Service: The staff are friendly and efficient, reflecting a deep respect for their patrons and the heritage of the restaurant. The service is straightforward, and while the pace can feel bustling during peak hours, it only adds to the charm of the place. Value: Given the quality and portion sizes, Pho Tàu Bay offers exceptional value for money. The prices are reasonable, and the generous servings leave you completely satisfied. Verdict: Pho Tàu Bay is a must-visit for anyone who craves authentic Vietnamese food and appreciates culinary traditions rooted in history. Whether you’re a first-timer or a longtime fan, the experience of dining here is like taking a delicious journey through time. The restaurant’s dedication to preserving its legacy makes it a shining gem in the Vietnamese culinary world.

address: 120 Nguyễn Thái Bình, Phường, Quận 1, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Pho is one of those dishes that becomes rather more complicated the moment you ask a local where to find the best one. In Vietnam, the divide between northern and southern pho is a serious matter, at least to those who have grown up eating it. Everyone has a preference, and almost everyone is convinced that the finest bowl is to be found somewhere suspiciously close to their childhood home. This is hardly a uniquely Vietnamese habit. Beijing has its zhajiangmian. Britain has fish and chips. Ask enough people about either and, sooner or later, someone will tell you that everything has gone downhill since the place they used to visit as a child changed hands. That is the problem with food so deeply rooted in everyday life: it is almost impossible to judge on flavour alone. The simpler the dish, the more memory gets involved. What people are defending is often not just a recipe, but a particular street, a particular kitchen, perhaps even a version of themselves that no longer exists. Which makes me slightly reluctant to declare any pho objectively good or bad. Still, I liked this place very much. What stood out was the beef, which had been treated with an unusual degree of precision. Different cuts were clearly distinguished, each bringing its own texture and character to the bowl. For all the apparent simplicity of pho, there was real attention to detail here — and, for me at least, it made a difference. Then there was the little girl in the first photograph, who registered my table before disappearing back to help with the cooking. She seemed remarkably young to be doing either, but went about it with the calm efficiency of someone who had been part of the rhythm of the place for far longer than her age suggested. Perhaps that is what I will remember most. Restaurants are rarely only about the food. Sometimes it is the small, unremarkable things — the people working around you, the rhythm of the room, the sense that this is simply another ordinary day for everyone except the traveller passing through — that give a meal its lasting flavour. As for whether this is the best pho in Vietnam, I have absolutely no intention of getting involved in that argument. The Vietnamese have been debating it for long enough without my assistance.

address: 120 Nguyễn Thái Bình, Phường, Quận 1, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: This place serves a very nostalgic, old-school Vietnamese comfort food experience. The atmosphere feels like stepping back in time—simple, lively, and full of local character. The broth is clear and light, with a gentle sweetness, and the beef balls are well-seasoned and satisfying. Overall flavors are clean and familiar rather than fancy, which is exactly the point. Prices are a bit higher than typical local spots, but that’s understandable given the location and the large number of tourists who come here. The restaurant is usually busy, with a mix of locals and visitors, creating a vibrant, slightly chaotic but enjoyable dining environment. It’s a great stop if you want to experience traditional Saigon-style food, especially if you’re visiting Vietnam for the first time or looking for a taste of “how it used to be.”

address: 120 Nguyễn Thái Bình, Phường, Quận 1, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: The "phở" we had were good, but did not give me the "omg I've got to have it again asap" impression. The broth was clean, not heavily spiced (some places put too much star anise which i don't like). The noodles were a bit thicker than what I like, but that is a preference. They gave you cooked beansprouts, lime, and three types of herbs (thai basil, and 2 different mints). The place was crowded since it was lunchtime, but the foods came out pretty quick once we put in our orders. The restaurant is one of those with no doors, but does have a back section on the left with a glass enclosure. There are fans from the walls l, but no A/C (at least not one I could feel). It seems to be a place where the locals eat so I think that is a plus. Overall, I would recommend this restaurant where anyone who wants to try a decent bowl of phở in Ben Thanh Ward. P.S. I forgot to take pictures the bowls before I ate it 🙃.

address: 120 Nguyễn Thái Bình, Phường, Quận 1, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: As a simple pho lover, I really enjoyed this place. I got a giant bowl of soup with three choices for meat. Pho is one of those foods that cash be done extremely well, but it might just not be your style, so people give it a loser score, despite being a great example of a specific taste. I imagine that's why most of the pho spots around town have a rating that hovers around 4.3 or 4.4, even tho they are high quality outlets.

address: 120 Nguyễn Thái Bình, Phường, Quận 1, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Not very glamorous place, no fancy interior but the pho is great. Soup base was good, not spicy. Service was quick and they accept card payments. Small Aircon dining area is available.

address: 52 Nguyễn Công Trứ, Thạnh Mỹ Tây, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: This was the first bowl of pho I had in Saigon and while I know it's more of tourist spot it was still a delicious experience. The staff were beyond friendly and the food was excellent. I ordered the chicken pho and because I'm Canadian of course I had to try the Photine which was yummy and an interesting fusion dish. I appreciated the backstory about matriarch Co Dung and her specific recipe and would recommend for anyone looking for a good meal and great atmosphere.

address: 52 Nguyễn Công Trứ, Thạnh Mỹ Tây, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: I ordered through the Grab becouse I didn't have time, but I must give review also at google maps! 🛵🛍️ The best Pho Bo what I have ever ate! 🥢🍜 I tried a lot of Pho Bo at Vietnam becouse I am Pho Bo lover but this one was the best!!! 🤌🥰 Especially the beef meat was so fresh, yummy and so soft! 🤤🥩 Believe me, I promise you can't do anything wrong when you order at this restaurant. Enough big portion (I bought big size soup with medium rare). The restaurant also send me separated garlic, vegetable, limet, chilli peppers, and chilli and brown sauce so I can add as I prefer. The chilli sauce was strong, be careful, but it is how it should be, good quality! 🌶️🤪 The fried rice was also amazing, very good spices! 🍚🧄🥚 I want moooore right now! 😋👌 Maybe just the portion of rice could be bigger for the price 90 000 VND, because rice is the cheapest food at Asia... 🫣 But I really like the taste of both of meals 👏 The pounched eggs with egg white was cooked enough so you don’t need to be worry for non-cooked egg 🥚👌 Thank you very much for your food 🥹🫶 My belly is happy!! 🤤🤰🏻

address: 52 Nguyễn Công Trứ, Thạnh Mỹ Tây, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: I really love the stir-fried eel glass noodles, served with a small bowl of soup. It’s one of Moon’s favorite dishes at this restaurant. My friend ordered the Phở, and she really liked it too! 🍜 The broth is slow-cooked from bones and meat, creating a naturally sweet, rich, and flavorful taste that stays true to traditional Northern Vietnamese Phở. If you’re looking for authentic Vietnamese food in Saigon, I definitely recommend giving this restaurant a try!

address: 52 Nguyễn Công Trứ, Thạnh Mỹ Tây, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Hands down one of the best pho I ever had! Soup is clean and light, yet fragrant and complex. The temperature of the soup just hot enough, I hate luke warm or overly boiling stock. This is just right and able to turn the raw beef into medium. The soup is so good, i finished it. Please do not forget to dip the beef into their home made garlic chili sauce.

address: 52 Nguyễn Công Trứ, Thạnh Mỹ Tây, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam

review_text: probably the busiest pho spot iv seen so far in vietnam these guys had a constant flow of customers coming and going, and the ladies were smashing out bowl after bowl, serving up all the customers! it was very impressive! the flavour was quite good as well. rich and full bodied. would definitely recommend coming here! especially if you want a late night pho session!

address: 1 Lê Lai, Bảy Hiền, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam

address: 1 Lê Lai, Bảy Hiền, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: A little hidden gem. We had one phở with flank brisket and one vegetarian one without meat. The taste of the broth was very delicious and the toppings are great. Fast and friendly service. Insta: @remotevagabond

address: 1 Lê Lai, Bảy Hiền, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Some of the best pho I’ve had in all of Vietnam; super aromatic broth, rich meat, perfect noodles, and efficient service. The alley setting and local crowd makes it feel like a perfect Saigon experience!

address: 1 Lê Lai, Bảy Hiền, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Tonight was my second time here. I still can’t find a better Phở bò đặc biệt for 65k. Good mix of meat and the bò viên (beef meatballs) is better than most places in VN. Pretty much my go to place for Phở while in Tân Bình / Tân Phú.

review_text: My wife and I were here this evening for a "Com Tam" or "Broken Rice" dinner as recommended by a local staff member at the hotel where we are staying at in Ho Chi Minh City - my wife and I are both first time visitors to Vietnam. And it turned out to be an excellent recommendation. We ordered the following: a Suon Nuong Bi Opla or grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, fried egg & broken rice, a Suon Nuong Bi Trung Kho or grilled pork chop, shredded pork skin, braised egg & broken rice, a Canh Kho Qua Don Thit or bitter melon w/ minced pork stuffing in a soup, a Dau Que Xao or stir-fried green beans, a Schweppes Soda, and a fresh coconut. The "Com Tam" sets were very, very good - yummy all in all. The "Canh" or soup was flavourful and the bitter melon with minced pork stuffing was delightful. Only the stir-fried green beans was average, but no complains whatsoever. My wife and I also oved the condiments that came with the meal (see photo herein). Service here was very good - very friendly and courteous. The dining ambience here was as good as it could be as it was not air-conditioned, but the place was well-ventilated. I highly recommend this place for an excellent "Com Tam" meal.

However, the quality of the rice and the traditional grilled pork ribs were excellent—tender and well-seasoned. That's definitely the highlight of this place.

review_text: I stopped by the restaurant after work, hungry, so I immediately ordered the fried chicken rice. The rice was hot, the fried chicken was golden and crispy, the meat inside was tender, and the sauce was rich and flavorful, typical of Southern Vietnamese cuisine – you'd nod in approval with every bite. However, to be honest: the food service was slow, especially when the restaurant was busy. The space is small and simple; going during peak hours can feel a bit cramped and noisy. On the plus side, the owner was friendly, enthusiastic, and pleasant to talk to, so the experience was still good. In short, this is the kind of restaurant where you "eat well, the price is reasonable, but patience is needed." If you prioritize flavor, it's definitely worth a try. However, if you're particular about time or a comfortable atmosphere, you should avoid peak hours.

review_text: Had the opportunity to try a few of their signature dishes, including the Eight Treasure Duck, Teochew-style Prawn Meatballs, and Spicy Duck Tongue. This place is truly a hidden gem in Saigon. I was genuinely impressed by the quality of the food — every dish was packed with flavour, showcased excellent wok hei, and reflected strong culinary skills from the kitchen team. The Eight Treasure Duck was rich and tender, the Teochew-style Prawn Meatballs were delightfully bouncy and tasty, while the Spicy Duck Tongue was perfectly seasoned with just the right kick. Bonus points go to the service crew, who were attentive, friendly, and provided top-notch service throughout the meal. If you’re visiting Saigon and looking for authentic Teochew-style cuisine, this restaurant is definitely worth a visit. Highly recommended! review_text: We had breakfast here on the morning we checked out of our hotel, and it was the perfect way to end our stay. The food selection was fantastic, with a great mix of traditional Vietnamese breakfast dishes and American breakfast options, which my husband really appreciated. Everything we ordered was fresh, high quality, and delicious. I also loved the drink selection, especially the Vietnamese iced coffee—it was so good! A special shoutout to Phat Huong who made our experience even better. He was incredibly kind, attentive, and consistently checked in to make sure we had everything we needed throughout our meal. Before we left, he even packaged a Vietnamese iced coffee for me to take on the go because he knew how much I enjoyed it. That thoughtful gesture really stood out and made us feel so well taken care of. The food was excellent, but the genuine hospitality made this place truly memorable. I would highly recommend dining here and would absolutely come back on my next visit.

review_text: The restaurant is located deep in an alley, so if you're going there, check Google Maps to find the right place to avoid getting lost or going too far. Usually, you'll find a fair near the turn-off from Duong Dinh Nghe street. The restaurant is quite easy to spot, with a large, attractive sign. The interior is spacious and comfortable. Since we were a large group, we chose a private room with air conditioning, and there were no extra charges. The restaurant looks clean, and the dishes and chopsticks on the table are neatly arranged. They mainly serve Chinese dishes; the ones we ordered weren't overly elaborate, but the preparation time was excessively long. Some dishes were even forgotten or the staff didn't know what we ordered, which was quite annoying. The food itself was average, nothing particularly special. Everything was heavily seasoned and greasy. The seasoning was so strong that the salmon had no flavor at all. The fried chicken wings smelled strongly of butter, like they'd put an entire jar of butter in them. The noodles and rice were decent, but the tofu was served last. The restaurant is okay if you like Chinese food and want to try it. But for me, it's not quite right.

review_text: Esta delivered a generally enjoyable meal, with the crab, pork jowl and Korean abalone starters all being solid. The standout was undoubtedly the duck, which was exceptional. Unfortunately, the spring lamb was chewy and came out less cooked than the medium doneness I requested. The two desserts were fairly ordinary, with nothing particularly memorable. Overall, there were some excellent dishes, but a few inconsistencies kept the experience from being truly outstanding.

address: 24/24 Đông Du, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: We truly enjoyed our dinner and experience. We took advantage of the tasting menu with the pairing wine. The food was flavourful, great presentation and the balance between the different courses. The wines were also well paired. Some were less to my taste, but all of them well matched with the food. The atmosphere was intimate and the service personalized. We appreciated that the restaurant is not too big and crowded. It was still busy, but it didn’t feel like it. It is dark, to make it more intimate, but we could easily see everything around us (even if I have an eye disability). Tam was the one with whom we mostly interacted. But everyone was friendly, professional and made sure we enjoyed our experience. I would not be surprised if we go back. Especially knowing they change the menu few times a year to adjust to the flavours of the seasons.

It feels very cozy and authentic. The Food: They have a great variety, serving both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options. Everything we ordered was freshly cooked and very delicious. It’s a good spot if you have a group with different diet needs. The Service: The staff wears modern Ao Dai that fits the traditional theme. However, the uniforms seemed a bit impractical for serving, as they were quite revealing when the staff leaned over to place food on the tables. Overall, it is a solid choice for a business dinner if you want a Vietnamese "Hometown" feel with fresh food.

address: 17 Lê Duẩn, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: We ate here on a Friday for dinner. We were welcomed and seated to our place. They initiated to put the napkin on our lap to use and offered water or sparkling water. They provided the copy of the meals we will be indulging. As starter meal, they gave us the com chat, it was unique since they use rice cracker as a base. Next is the Vietnamese pomelo salad with herbs and mud crab. Cannot taste fully the crab but the pomelo blend and cleanse our palette. Next we had is the bap xao which taste like the banh Trang but with softer wrapper. The beans ensure it is warm while we ate. Next is the cha bio which we thought it was a normal spring roll but it wasn’t. It tasted like corned beef inside the wrapper dipped in a mild chili sauce. Next is the main course, it was Bo luc lac which is fried Australian wagyu beef. It was so soft and doesn’t require you to chew too much. The taste of the sauce is similar to some dishes in Philippines like caldereta but more herby side. Lastly, the barramundi which tasted good. We didn’t expect it was a fish except for the sauce which has a strong fish smell but the crew prompt as she served to us. The herb on top help us to not taste the fish. Overall, the food was great but not so great that you want to come back and eat again.

review_text: Had a wonderful dining experience at Niêu House! The food was absolutely delicious, especially the traditional clay pot dishes which were rich in flavor and beautifully presented. The service was excellent — staff were friendly, attentive, and very professional. The restaurant has a beautiful, quiet, and cozy atmosphere, perfect for relaxing meals with family or friends. Prices are reasonable for the quality offered. Highly recommended!

restaurant_name: Nhà hàng Cơm Niêu - Niêu House (Nieu House Authentic Vietnam Claypot Rice Restaurant)
address: 122 Cao Thắng, Bàn Cờ, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Visited January 2nd 2026. Had salted hen chicken, Yam soup, stir fried garlic broccoli and crispy rice. The food was delicious but the service was strange. Even though everything was supposed to be coming together except maybe the soup should have been served first, they brought the rice by itself and it sat there for about 15 minutes. And they brought the broccoli, then about 10 minutes later, the chicken. But I still recommend this place as everything was delicious.

restaurant_name: Nhà hàng Cơm Niêu - Niêu House (Nieu House Authentic Vietnam Claypot Rice Restaurant)
address: 122 Cao Thắng, Bàn Cờ, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: This six-story restaurant offers a unique dining experience with various spaces tailored to different moods and occasions. The private rooms, perfect for intimate gatherings or special celebrations, provide an exclusive feel with stylish decor and attentive service. The menu showcases a blend of traditional and contemporary dishes. The flavours are bold yet balanced, and the portions are generous. Whether hosting a small party or enjoying a quiet meal with friends, the ambience and food quality make this spot a standout choice for casual and special occasions.

restaurant_name: Nhà hàng Cơm Niêu - Niêu House (Nieu House Authentic Vietnam Claypot Rice Restaurant)

review_text: Food is good. But the management has some serious issues. I ordered the lunch set as in the picture, priced at 289k and confirmed with the waiter. Later they said one dish ran out so switched to another similar dish. When paying the bill, the manager dramatically told me that the “set” we ordered from the picture is not a set, it’s just for “displaying the promotion”, so we need to pay at original price. After a few iterations of explaining, the manager finally agreed to let us pay the set price as in the picture plus price of the replacement dish (note that one dish is missing from the set but we still paid for it). This is clearly a mistake of their side, although I’m not sure it’s intentional or not (hopefully not). But it’s really frustrating that the manager didn’t admit any mistake at all and just let the customer pay for the restaurant’s mistake. —— this is the wrong way to do business.

review_text: A Memorable Birthday Breakfast at The Lounge We recently visited The Lounge at the Sheraton to celebrate a family birthday, and it was a truly wonderful experience. The bar on the 23rd floor does the best cocktails with the most amazing flavours I've ever experienced (also has 2 for 1 happy hour with Sheraton/Marriott membership). address: 80 Đông Du, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Loved our stay at Sheraton Grand Opera hotel. The staff are attentive and friendly and have looked after us with grace and charm. We especially loved our experience at the lounge bar and Nhu was a brilliant addition to the overall atmosphere. Would not hesitate to stay here again

address: 80 Đông Du, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Certainly! The Lounge at Sheraton Saigon Hotel & Towers is a delightful place to meet, work, and unwind. Cuisine: The Lounge offers a diverse menu that spans international and Vietnamese flavours. Whether you’re craving pastries, cakes, or local comfort food, this modern ambience caters to all tastes. We got complimentary tea during our stay at Sheraton Saigon. It was a great surprise as they gave so much variety of pastries, muffins macrons &small snacks. We had ordered English breakfast and Earl Grey tea. Tea was rejuvenating. Lounge staff VY helped us a lot she packed our food as we couldn’t eat all the snacks. She packed extra two pastries too 🥰. Truly that day we didn’t eat dinner as tea was so good. Special thanks to VY for her help. review_text: An excellent place to spend an evening. Light music, happy faces, helpful staff that pays attention. But wait, that’s not the best part. Best part is Ha. Who mixes best cocktails to die for. Thank you Ha!!!

address: 91 Mạc Thị Bưởi, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: We had an incredible experience at The Monkey Gallery Dining. Every dish was delicious, creative and beautifully presented, with some really interesting combinations of Vietnamese flavours and premium ingredients. The tasting menu was very generous and by the end we were absolutely full! Despite the number of courses, each dish felt unique and thoughtfully put together. The service and overall experience were just as impressive as the food. We honestly couldn’t have asked for a better evening. Definitely one of the highlights of our time in Saigon and a meal we’ll remember for a long time. Highly recommended!

address: 91 Mạc Thị Bưởi, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: One of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve had. The Monkey Gallery Dining completely exceeded my expectations. Every dish was incredibly creative, beautifully presented, and full of flavors I had never experienced before. The tasting menu feels like a culinary journey where each plate tells a story. The balance of flavors, textures, and presentation is simply outstanding. The staff was exceptional—professional, attentive, and passionate about explaining every dish and ingredient. They truly elevate the whole experience. This restaurant easily made it into my top 5 dining experiences in the world. Everything was flawless from start to finish. If you’re visiting Ho Chi Minh City and enjoy fine dining, this place is an absolute must. Worth every minute and every bite.

address: 91 Mạc Thị Bưởi, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Last dinner before leaving Vietnam and it was a perfect way to end it! All the dishes are amazing and the drinks as well! Our server Tommy was also very knowledgable and friendly! They even gave us free course as well as a partin gift! 10/10 would go again

address: 91 Mạc Thị Bưởi, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: It took them three hours to finish serving us even when we always finished our dishes very quickly, since there were long wait times in between. The portions were too small. We appreciate the staff's effort but the service was presumptuous and rigid in a few aspects. Fyi, there's only one set menu. Not vegetarian or vegan friendly at all.

address: 91 Mạc Thị Bưởi, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Amazing experience at Monkey Gallery. The atmosphere is stylish and relaxed, and you can really feel the attention to quality and detail in every part of the restaurant. The highlight for me was the Rabbit Morel. The rabbit was incredibly tender and perfectly cooked, paired with rich, earthy morels that gave the dish a deep, elegant flavor. Beautifully balanced and absolutely delicious. Definitely a place worth visiting if you appreciate refined, well-executed food.

restaurant_name: Quán Bụi - Lê Thánh Tôn - Authentic Vietnamese Cuisine
address: 222 - 224 Lê Thánh Tôn, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Quán Bụi continues to remind me why Vietnamese cuisine is so loved. From the moment you walk in, you're greeted by a warm, nostalgic atmosphere that blends traditional Vietnamese charm with a modern dining experience. The food was outstanding. The roasted chicken was crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, the crispy beef was packed with flavour, and the stir-fried glass noodles with prawns were perfectly seasoned with a generous amount of fresh ingredients. We ended the meal with fried banana and ice cream, which was the perfect sweet finish. What impressed me most was that despite the restaurant being busy, the service remained attentive, friendly, and efficient. Every dish arrived well presented and was served at a comfortable pace. If you're looking for authentic Vietnamese cuisine in Ho Chi Minh City with a welcoming ambience, consistently good food, and excellent service, Quán Bụi is definitely worth a visit. I'll certainly be returning the next time I'm back in the city.

restaurant_name: Quán Bụi - Lê Thánh Tôn - Authentic Vietnamese Cuisine
address: 222 - 224 Lê Thánh Tôn, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Quán Bụi Central, Quán Bụi Original, and the Quán Bụi restaurant chain are places I have visited month after month, year after year—and I truly believe they represent some of the very best Vietnamese cuisine. They offer outstanding, flavorful, and authentic dishes, served in a warm and inviting atmosphere by genuinely courteous staff. Everything is thoughtfully prepared and beautifully presented, delivering real pleasure to anyone who appreciates Vietnamese cuisine—and great food in general. The ingredients are consistently fresh, the ambiance is refined yet unpretentious, and there is none of the unnecessary noise or excessive ceremony often found elsewhere. These restaurants embody authenticity and sincerity, offering a truly genuine culinary experience. They provide one of the most faithful and enjoyable introductions to the food and culture of this remarkable country—an experience I wholeheartedly recommend to anyone visiting Ho Chi Minh City, and to anyone who truly understands and values the pleasure of authentic, beautifully crafted cuisine.

address: 59 Hồ Xuân Hương, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Authentic Vietnamese flavours not found back home. The ambience is amazing, with old French colonial architecture. It’s crammed with people during peak hours, but the food is great.

address: 59 Hồ Xuân Hương, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Quite a nice restaurant from Tân Hải Vân Group, which owns several more restaurants within the city. This restaurant itself has been around for 25 years already! It has an outdoor dining area accompanied by live music, and an indoor dining area that looks like a traditional Vietnamese house. The theme of the restaurant is Vietnamese village culture, both in its cooking and its aesthetics. There’s a huge menu with a bunch of selections to choose from. The dishes here are ones you typically eat with rice at home. It’s most famous for its clay pot rice, which is the best way to cook rice, the traditional Vietnamese method or cooking rice, and the restaurant name itself. Our order: • Gỏi Sứa (Jellyfish Salad) 178.000 VND • Đậu Hũ Hoàng Kim (Fried tofu with salted egg yolk) 98.000 VND • Cá Bống Mú (Grouper) MARKETPRICE • Cơm Đập (charcoal grilled rice in clay pot) 50.000 VND • Cơm Niêu (Steamed rice in clay pot) 30.000 VND We bought a grouper and asked for it to be made into a caramelized dish and a sour soup dish. This was eaten with the clay pot rice. The sauce and small lard pieces in the caramelized dish could also be eaten with the grilled rice. Prices are on the higher end, but not bad. Service is nice and friendly. Restaurant is aesthetic and comfortable. Food tastes good! My favourite here is the fried tofu with salted egg yolk!

address: 59 Hồ Xuân Hương, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: A great introduction to classic Vietnamese home-style cooking. While we didn’t order the clay-pot rice this time, it’s still an experience in itself watching the staff crack open the clay pots and send them flying across the restaurant adds a lot of theatre and energy to the meal. The dishes we did have were full of flavour, comforting, and well executed, with a real sense of tradition behind them. Service was attentive and efficient, and while the atmosphere is lively rather than polished, it suits the style of food perfectly. A solid spot for an authentic, no-frills Vietnamese dining experience.

address: 59 Hồ Xuân Hương, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Not great. Food was good but small serving. Our waitress told us our first few choices were sold out and then prawn dishes would take 30 - 45 minutes and then walked off before we finished our order. Not a nice experience.

The waitstaff are always helpful, knowledgeable, attentive, and polite. The restaurant is always nice, clean, and pleasant. It could be very crowded at times but not chaotic. It is a bit more expensive than the average restaurants in Sài Gòn, but with AC, nice settings, hygiene, pleasant environment I think it's more than worth it. Highly recommended 👌

review_text: This restaurant didn’t live up to the hype. Nothing about it was necessarily bad but nothing was that great that I would choose it again over other options. The food was seasoned poorly and the portion sizes small relative to the prices. The service was quite slow even though the tables were not all taken. address: 196 Lê Thánh Tôn, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: The restaurant may be small, but it doesn’t feel cramped. There are tables for both groups and solo diners, plus a balcony with a beautiful, airy view overlooking Ben Thanh Market. The seafood is fresh, with live tanks where you can see it swimming. The dishes are well-prepared and delicious — the fried rice is not greasy at all. The staff are very polite and attentive, and the prices are reasonable considering its central location. Overall, I think this place is definitely worth trying.

address: 31-33 Đặng Dung, Tân Định, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Had an incredible dining experience at À by T.U.N.G in HCMC! Every dish is a pleasant surprise with stunning presentation and outstanding flavors. The appetizers are like edible art. The caviar bites are fresh and bright, while the oysters with zesty green sauce taste pure and ocean‑fresh. Each creative bite brings unexpected texture layers that wow your taste buds. The steak is perfectly cooked, tender and juicy with rich sauce. The salmon roe rice bowl is savory and comforting. Desserts are the perfect finish — well‑balanced, refreshing and never overly sweet. Every course shows the chef’s brilliant creativity. High‑quality ingredients, refined seasoning and thoughtful combinations make the whole meal full of wonderful surprises. Great atmosphere and attentive service. Huge thanks to the restaurant for the lovely complimentary birthday dessert, which made my special day even more memorable. A must‑visit fine‑dining spot in HCMC!

address: 31-33 Đặng Dung, Tân Định, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: We booked the whole restaurant to celebrate our anniversary, so our experience may have been a little different from a regular evening. The team catered to our whole group incredibly well, and everyone felt genuinely looked after. They helped take care of the setup, served the food and drinks with great attention, and explained each course clearly as it arrived. The staff were patient, warm, and helpful throughout the night. There were many small details to manage with a group our size, but everything ran smoothly and the pacing felt comfortable. We never felt rushed. The chef’s creativity was one of the highlights for me. Every course felt carefully considered, from the combination of flavors to the plating, tableware, and decorative details. I loved seeing Vietnamese ingredients and familiar ideas presented in such an inventive and refined way. The restaurant itself was spotless, intimate, and upscale, while still feeling cozy and comfortable. The flowers, lighting, glassware, and overall setup made our anniversary feel even more special. We had an amazing evening at Å by TUNG. I am very grateful to the chef and the entire team for the care they put into our celebration and for looking after our whole group so well.

address: 31-33 Đặng Dung, Tân Định, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Å by Tung delivers a thoroughly pleasant fine-dining experience. The atmosphere is calm, refined, and thoughtfully designed, comfortable without being stiff. Service was attentive and well-paced, making the evening feel relaxed rather than rushed. The food is creative and confident. Each course shows clear intent and technical skill, with flavors that are interesting without being gimmicky. Overall, it’s a very enjoyable culinary journey. One small note: the portions are more generous than what one might typically expect from a tasting menu. That said, this is more a reflection of my own capacity than any fault of the kitchen: the quality and execution remain excellent throughout. All in all, a memorable and satisfying experience. Would happily recommend for those who enjoy creative cuisine and a polished dining atmosphere.

address: 31-33 Đặng Dung, Tân Định, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: While doing a Michelin restaurant tour, A by TUNG was one of the best dining experiences I've had by far. The service was great and the food was so amazingly balanced & beautifully presented. The 16 course set menu contrasted flavours and textures exceptionally well. Each course built up anticipation and the non-alcoholic pairings complemented each group of courses. I was told their menu is seasonal, so what I ate might not be on your menu, but that makes me even more excited to return in the future. Thank you to the team for the wonderful experience and I hope to dine at your establishment on my next trip to Vietnam.

address: 31-33 Đặng Dung, Tân Định, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: An absolute masterclass in modern fine dining. From the moment we stepped into Å by TUNG, the atmosphere was intimate, sophisticated, and welcoming. The tasting menu is a brilliant journey; every course was a meticulously crafted piece of art that balanced bold, innovative flavors with deep respect for local Vietnamese ingredients. While the entire experience was exceptional, the Northern-style Pho was an absolute standout—perfectly balanced and deeply flavorful. The Mekong Delta-inspired Canh Chua was equally impressive, offering a unique and elevated take on the classic soup that I won’t soon forget. It’s rare to find a kitchen that executes both technical precision and soulful storytelling so flawlessly. The staff were incredibly attentive, providing thoughtful explanations of the ingredients and inspiration behind each dish without ever feeling intrusive. This isn’t just dinner; it’s a truly memorable experience. Whether you’re a local foodie or visiting Ho Chi Minh City, this place is an absolute must-visit. Five stars are well-deserved—I am already looking forward to my next visit to see what Chef Tùng and his team create next.

review_text: Exceptional Fine Dining with Spectacular Showmanship – A Must-Visit in Saigon: Ho Chi Minh City is evolving rapidly, and its culinary scene is expanding in incredible ways. On my recent visit, I wanted to see how HCMC delivers a true high-end, fine dining experience. I was looking for something exceptional near my hotel and chose Cloud Nine, located on the 11th floor of the La Siesta Hotel. Knowing via Google that it is an LGBTQ+-friendly establishment completely sealed the deal for me, perfectly reflecting the young, progressive, and welcoming vibe I discovered throughout this vibrant city. From start to finish, the attention to detail here is world-class. I opted for "The Elegance" set menu, and the presentation and pacing were spectacular. The culinary journey began with a delightful Salsa Chicken Tartlet starter, followed by a beautifully prepared Bacon-Wrapped Seabass and a rich, velvety Creamy Truffle Mushroom soup. The absolute highlight of the night, however, was the main course: the Premium Australian Tenderloin. It was prepared tableside with incredible showmanship by my server, Bao. He is an absolute professional—exceptionally trained, attentive, and passionate about his craft. (Sadly, my video only started recording after his performance, but the memory of it definitely stuck!) The top-tier hospitality didn't stop there; the manager, Tin, also personally stopped by my table to ensure every single detail of the evening was flawless. While I’ve seen a few reviews online mentioning smaller portion sizes, I found the multi-course progression to be incredibly satiating due to the rich, complex layers of flavor in every single dish. Make no mistake, Cloud Nine is a premium, high-end establishment and not a budget option—nor should it be. The level of execution, atmosphere, and service is elite. In fact, I have easily paid triple the price for a comparable dining experience in major food cities like Los Angeles and San Francisco. For the sheer quality of food, ambiance, and care you receive, Cloud Nine delivers phenomenal value. I cannot recommend it highly enough.

address: 180-188 Lý Tự Trọng, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: We just had the BEST dining ever... Cloud 9 Rooftop Restaurant, the set menu was fab and just US$63 per person. What a grand performance and delicious food. Highly recommend if you are ever in Saigon and want a special meal it is the place to go. We bought our ticket on Klook and it included a bottle of wine, how could you go wrong. All the courses were amazing, and the staff wonderful. Francis our main server was just the best cooking our steak to perfection with an amazing display not to be missed when you are visiting Saigon. Video attached.

address: 180-188 Lý Tự Trọng, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Exceptional Ambiance with a Standard Culinary Profile Cloud Nine offers a sophisticated dining environment that undoubtedly serves as its greatest asset. The atmosphere is exceptional, providing a refined and elegant backdrop that is perfectly suited for special occasions or high-level business dinners. This is further complemented by impeccable service, with a team that is both professional and attentive to detail. The culinary experience, however, presents a more nuanced story. While the set menus such as the “Elegance” and “Essence” series are well-structured and technically competent, the execution remains within a relatively safe and standard territory. Dishes like the Aussie Tenderloin Beef Rossini and the Seared Norwegian Salmon are enjoyable and correctly prepared, yet they lack the distinctive “wow” factor or creative flair one might expect at this price point and prestige. Overall, Cloud Nine is a premier choice for those prioritizing a superior vibe and professional service. While the food is solid and dependable, it serves more as a secondary accompaniment to the stunning surroundings rather than a standalone culinary destination.

address: 180-188 Lý Tự Trọng, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: If I could give 100 stars I would. The staff were all incredible! So friendly and helpful with everything. The food was amazing! The fire show with the wagyu was the nicest surprise and the whole dinner was just perfection. If you want an incredible night of food, wine and relaxing atmosphere, look no further.

address: 180-188 Lý Tự Trọng, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Unforgettable Valentine’s Dinner with a View 🥂✨ My partner and I spent Valentine’s Day at Cloud Nine Restaurant, located on the 11th floor of the La Siesta Hotel, and it was truly a world-class experience. From the moment we arrived, the sophisticated Western-style ambiance and the warm welcome set the stage for a perfect evening. The Food: The culinary quality here is exceptional. Main Courses: I had the striploin, which was cooked to perfection, served with creamy mashed potatoes and a rich, flavorful red wine sauce. My partner opted for the truffle pasta, which was incredibly fragrant and indulgent. Desserts: We finished on a high note with a decadent chocolate mousse and a classic crème brûlée. Both were beautifully presented (as you can see in the photos!) and tasted as good as they looked. The Experience: We were lucky enough to be seated right by the window, offering a breathtaking panoramic view of the Saigon skyline. Watching the city lights while enjoying such high-quality service made the night feel incredibly special. The staff was attentive and professional, ensuring that "service" wasn't just a word, but a priority. Verdict: If you are looking for a romantic spot in Ho Chi Minh City that combines high-end Western cuisine with an unbeatable atmosphere, this is it. The heart-shaped decorations and the attention to detail for Valentine’s Day were the cherry on top. Overall: A perfect evening. We will definitely be back!

address: 3 Nguyễn Huệ, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: I visited Matsuri on the strength of the reviews and I couldn’t be more disappointed in every possible way. Here is an honest account, you can thank me later :) The menu is promising with lots of coloured pictures of fun options. The reality is more sober. This is not a sushi restaurant with a sushi chef, it is sushi assembly. They obviously buy things processed in a factory and assemble them and reheat them upon order. Most food came in under 20 seconds if that says anything. Fish freshness is poor. It won’t make you sick but it’s borderline. Nigiri has way too much yucky rice. Sashimi is limp and aged. Salads were flavourless and yet over salted. Chawanmushi was nasty. See the faulty machine separation in my pic? See the indecipherable factory thing on the chawanmushi? The ginger was dyed pink. Wasabi had no semblance of spice. To add to the terrible food, the ambiance was awful. The attached video is a symphony of cutlery sorting that they did for 20 minutes. Obnoxious! The staff also disappeared and needed to be fetched every time. The place is an echo chamber for sound with big groups of office people cackling. You’d be best to steer clear of this place when there are countless excellent options nearby in Japantown just a few minutes east. You’re welcome!
