address: 37bis Ký Con, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Quince was genuinely one of the best meals I’ve ever had—and probably the single best meal of our entire trip through Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam. The service was easily the best we experienced anywhere. Everyone was incredibly quick, friendly, attentive, and polished without ever making the evening feel stiff or overly formal. Their sommelier-in-training was fantastic as well: knowledgeable, genuinely enthusiastic, and extremely helpful. We had a glass of Pinot Noir that paired beautifully with the meal. The food was unbelievable from beginning to end. The whipped tofu and tomato dish was one of the biggest surprises of the night—bright, rich, perfectly balanced, and an absolute must-order. The duck was extraordinary, with genuinely the best, crispiest duck skin I have ever had. Even the bread and accompaniments were memorable, which tells you how much thought goes into every detail here. Dessert somehow maintained the same level. The dark-chocolate dessert with chocolate sorbet was completely outrageous: deeply chocolatey without becoming heavy, beautifully presented, and easily one of the best desserts of the trip. Quince’s wood-fired cooking, seasonal ingredients, and combination of Mediterranean influence, Asian flavors, and French technique are apparent throughout the menu. Its continued recognition by the Michelin Guide makes complete sense. An extraordinary restaurant with phenomenal cooking, exceptional hospitality, and a team that clearly cares about every part of the experience. Do not miss this place in Ho Chi Minh City.

address: 37bis Ký Con, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Another Michelin-recommended restaurant that truly lives up to its reputation. Every dish was executed exceptionally well, from the perfectly cooked steak to the classic combination of bone marrow and caviar. The oysters were incredibly fresh, and the accompanying sauce enhanced their natural sweetness beautifully. The octopus was cooked to perfection, with an excellent texture and flavor. The desserts were equally impressive and provided a memorable finish to the meal. Even the petit fours served at the end reflected the restaurant’s attention to detail and commitment to quality. Overall, this is a restaurant that is absolutely worth making a special trip for.

address: 37bis Ký Con, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: A massive congratulations to the entire team at Quince for your well-deserved inclusion in Tatler’s Best 20. Having visited several times in the past and also this April, we can safely say that Quince remains our favorite restaurant in the world. The food is, quite simply, sublime. Each dish a testament to the artistry in your kitchen. But beyond the flavors, it is the warmth and professionalism of the staff that truly sets you apart. A heartfelt thank you to Julien, Matthew, Nikki, Quin, Alex, and the rest of the team for making every visit unforgettable. We already counting down the days until we can return and couldn't recommend higher. Leigh & Tammy

review_text: Dirty cramped alley and no free seating available. There are multiple vendors there selling everything from bot chien (fried dough with scrambled eggs), sup cua (crab soup), spring rolls, banh canh cua (crab noodles), banh khot (think bite sized banh xeo), snails, and corn. I got banh khot, spring rolls and banh canh cua. The first two dishes were below average. The banh canh (30k vnd) was good though. There is no seating available other than some stools at the back of the alley near the motorbike parking and near the snail vendor. It looked like communal seating, but the snail vendor has employees that will force you to buy beverages from them in order to sit down. It seems a bit ridiculous to monopolize the seating like that and to charge as much as other vendors do for food. Traffic in the alley is cramped between food traffic from customers, motorbike drivers, and garbagemen dragging rubbish dumpsters dripping with filthy water inches away from your table and stool. If you're not a cat person I'd stay away as well because stray kittens will go underneath all the tables looking for scraps.

address: Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 72400, Việt Nam
review_text: This is a fantastic restaurant that offers authentic Vietnamese cuisine from all three regions—North, Central, and South. The flavors are rich and true to traditional cooking styles, making it a great place to experience the diverse culinary heritage of Vietnam. I had the chance to try a variety of dishes, and overall, I was extremely satisfied. The food was well-seasoned, perfectly cooked, and presented beautifully. The highlight of the meal was the signature “cơm niêu” (clay pot rice), which had a crispy outer layer and a fragrant, fluffy texture inside. It paired wonderfully with other dishes, especially the braised meat and seafood options. The menu featured many traditional Vietnamese favorites. The stir-fried vegetables were fresh and cooked just right, retaining their natural sweetness and crunch. The braised pork and fish in clay pots were flavorful, rich, and tender, absorbing the seasonings well. One of the most unique dishes was the purple yam soup, which had a striking color and a naturally sweet, earthy taste. The hot and sour soup with fish was another standout, balancing tanginess, spice, and umami flavors in a way that made it incredibly comforting. Despite ordering a lot of food, my group of three managed to finish everything, which speaks to how delicious each dish was. The portions were generous yet not overwhelming, allowing us to try a variety of flavors without feeling too heavy. The atmosphere of Cơm Niêu Đầu is warm and welcoming, with a rustic yet clean and comfortable setting. It feels like a home-style Vietnamese dining experience, which adds to the charm. The service was attentive and efficient, with staff making sure we had everything we needed throughout the meal. This restaurant is definitely a place I will revisit every time I return to Vietnam. The authentic flavors, quality ingredients, and skillful cooking make it a must-try for anyone who appreciates Vietnamese cuisine. Whether you're looking for a nostalgic taste of home or an introduction to traditional Vietnamese food, Cơm Niêu Đẩu is a top choice in Ho Chi Minh City.

address: Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 72400, Việt Nam

address: 11 Sư Vạn Hạnh, Hòa Hưng, Hồ Chí Minh 720000, Việt Nam
review_text: I recently visited this restaurant for a Wednesday dinner, and to be honest, I left feeling quite frustrated. Despite being a Vietnamese-style buffet, I was pleasantly surprised to see a Sashimi counter. It’s an interesting concept to blend local flavors with Japanese cuisine, but unfortunately, the execution and service fell far short of expectations. I definitely won't be returning. 1. Unprofessional Service at the Sashimi Counter Sashimi is my favorite, and while the fish itself was actually quite fresh, the service was a nightmare. When I first approached the counter, the employee refused to serve me, claiming she wasn't "responsible" for that specific section. She insisted I wait for the person in charge. It was only after another employee stepped in and pushed her to help that I finally got my food. This kind of buck-passing in front of a customer is incredibly unprofessional. 2. Lackluster Grilled Seafood & Meat The grilled section was a major letdown. The seafood was cold, small, and lacked flavor. It felt like it had been sitting out for a long time. Furthermore, the variety was non-existent; there was no grilled pork or beef—only chicken. It seems the kitchen only focuses on steamed crab and shrimp, leaving the grill options neglected and unappetizing. 3. Poor Table Maintenance Even though it was a Wednesday night and not particularly crowded, the staff failed to clear my table. Every time I returned with a new plate, my old, dirty dishes were still sitting there. There was no proactive service at all. Final Verdict: While the idea of a Vietnamese buffet offering sashimi is a nice touch, the poor management of the grill station and the dismissive attitude of the staff made for a bad experience. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and trains their staff to be more helpful and attentive.

address: 11 Sư Vạn Hạnh, Hòa Hưng, Hồ Chí Minh 720000, Việt Nam
review_text: We highly recommend this restaurant for the delicious food AND excellent service. We explored the expansive mall and We came for lunch on a Monday . The staff warmly greeted us and our servers were very attentive. The food is AMAZING. The Ga chien nuoc Mam is the BEST chicken wings I’ve had anywhere. Crispy, juicy, and oh so FLAVORFUL! I don’t usually go to Buffets for chicken wings , but I’m so happy we found this at Hoang Yen ! The grilled whole shrimp, clams and oc were also very delicious and they make sure it’s constantly replenished . Hoang Yen buffet has a good selection of authentic Vietnamese dishes, not just the usual seafood . Banh khot, Banh xeo,hot vit Lon,etc….This restaurant is top notch in food and service . It took us about a 25 min GRAB ride from Landmark 81 area - definitely worth it and we will be doing it again soon!

review_text: A Fantastic Vietnam Buffet Experience! Its always HY buffet every time in HCMC! The variety of dishes offered was impressive, featuring an authentic spread of Vietnamese cuisine, from fresh spring rolls to delicious grilled meats and seafood. The highlight for me was the seafood station, and I could customize it with my preferred toppings. The steam fish was another standout—soft on the inside, and filled with well-seasoned ingredients. The selection of dipping sauces, perfectly complemented the dishes. The ambiance was warm and inviting, with a touch of Vietnamese charm in the decor. The staff was attentive and friendly, ensuring that everything was replenished and that guests had a great dining experience. To top it off, the dessert section featured an array of traditional Vietnamese delicacies, making for a perfect ending to a fantastic meal. Overall, this buffet is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic Vietnamese flavors. The combination of fresh ingredients, great variety, and excellent service makes it well worth the visit!

address: Bến thuyền qua Mars Venus, 9A Đ. Trần Văn Trà, Nhà Bè, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Overall great place for a date or special occasion, but food leaves something to be desired. The atmosphere is quite pleasant. You arrive by boat and enter the restaurant through another restaurant. All the tables and chairs are adorned with nice LED lights, enhancing the ambiance. We ordered one of the set menus. The salad was definitely the highlight of the meal. The soup was pretty good, but the two main courses left something to be desired. The pasta noodles were enjoyable, but the sauce was overly strong, and the shrimp was overcooked. We also had the duck, which had good flavor but was far too dry. The scallop was quite good—I really enjoyed its texture; it wasn’t soft but had a pleasant chewiness. The steak was decent with good flavor, though it was too chewy. The grits served with the steak were interesting, somewhat like a localized version of grits. The best part of the steak dish was the roasted garlic—it was some of the best I’ve ever had. Its consistency was perfect, and the flavor wasn’t overpowering; I could’ve eaten the whole bulb myself. For dessert, we had the cheesecake and molten lava cake. The molten lava cake was just okay and not very molten—it would’ve been much better with vanilla ice cream on the side. The so-called New York-style cheesecake was neither New York-style, nor cheesecake, nor even a cake. It was more like a cookie crumble topped with sweet cream and a layer of pistachios or nuts. The taste was decent, but if you’re expecting cheesecake, it’s nowhere close. It should be renamed to something else. We were also given a call server button to request service, but it didn’t work at all. When we pointed this out, they didn’t bother replacing it.

restaurant_name: Garden in Island by Mars Venus

The team was attentive without being intrusive, which created a very natural and elegant experience. A perfect place for a dinner, a quiet meeting, or simply to enjoy a moment away from the energy of the city. Highly recommended for anyone looking for something aesthetic, relaxing, and genuinely well curated. ✨

Whatever you do, do not skip the house fries! They’re ridiculously good and crisp. Pair all of that with their handcrafted, delicious cocktails, and you’ve got the perfect night out. Great music, awesome atmosphere, and friendly staff. Highly recommended!

Definitely worth coming to for spectacular views.

address: 38 Nguyễn Ư Dĩ, St, An Khánh, Hồ Chí Minh 10000, Việt Nam
review_text: I visited Ho Chi Minh City and celebrate a friend's birthday, and we decided to dine at this beautiful fine dining restaurant by the riverside. It turned out to be one of the highlights of our trip. The atmosphere was elegant, the view was stunning, and the service was truly outstanding. The staff were warm, attentive, and knowledgeable. They took the time to introduce the menu and recommended several signature dishes based on our preferences. The pork ribs were absolutely the best I have ever had. They were incredibly tender, juicy, and perfectly cooked, with a wonderful balance of lean meat and fat that melted in my mouth. When the restaurant found out that we were celebrating a birthday, they kindly surprised us with a complimentary slice of cake. It was such a thoughtful gesture that made the celebration even more special. We truly appreciated their hospitality and attention to detail. Thank you for giving us such a memorable dining experience. I will definitely come back to this restaurant the next time I visit Ho Chi Minh City, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for excellent food, amazing service, and a wonderful riverside atmosphere.

address: 38 Nguyễn Ư Dĩ, St, An Khánh, Hồ Chí Minh 10000, Việt Nam
review_text: The Deck Saigon is one of the most beautiful riverside restaurants in Ho Chi Minh City. With its peaceful location along the Saigon River, it offers a relaxing atmosphere that’s perfect for a romantic dinner, a special celebration, or simply enjoying a meal with friends. The restaurant serves a mix of Vietnamese and international dishes, all beautifully presented with fresh ingredients. The food was delicious, and the cocktails were well made. While the prices are on the higher side, the quality of the food, excellent service, and stunning riverside views make the experience worthwhile. If possible, visit around sunset to enjoy the changing colours of the sky and the city lights reflecting on the river. The ambience becomes even more magical in the evening. Overall, The Deck Saigon offers a memorable dining experience. It’s definitely worth visiting if you’re looking for great food, a relaxing atmosphere, and one of the best waterfront views in Ho Chi Minh City.

Marriott members receive 10% discount here. Definitely we will visit repeatedly for happy Sundays.

address: Le Méridien Saigon, 3C Tôn Đức Thắng, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: I had great time with my mom on Xmas eve in this restaurant. address: Le Méridien Saigon, 3C Tôn Đức Thắng, Sài Gòn, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam

Portions were generous without being overwhelming, and there was a good variety on the menu to suit different tastes.

The food is just okay for its price range. 3 of us have different options from the lunch menu, but the only dish I enjoy is the turkey with a luscious balance of tenderness and chewiness. I have rather a sweet tooth and am most often quite easy with dessert offerings, but I did not enjoy the dishes here at all, which taste like your $2 convenience store cakes.

address: 76 Lê Lai, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Beautiful Restaurant, Excellent Service, Disappointing Food After my massage, I was looking for a high-end dim sum restaurant, and Black Vinegar at New World Hotel had great reviews, so we decided to try it. The restaurant is beautiful, elegant, and luxurious. We loved the interior design, and the reception staff made us feel very welcome. The service throughout our meal was outstanding. Special thanks to Châu, Nhi, Tân, and Bích for being so professional, friendly, and attentive. Unfortunately, the food didn’t match the beautiful setting. Although they used real crab meat, the dim sum wasn’t memorable. The wrappers were too thick and firm instead of soft and silky like you would expect from a high-end restaurant. Most dishes lacked flavor, the vegetables were too bitter, the truffle abalone was too bland, and the har gow had a fishy taste. The ginger kumquat drink was good, but the passion fruit drink was too sour. The mango dessert was the best dish, although I would suggest using less grapefruit because it made the dessert slightly bitter. In my opinion, Dim Tu Tac, Yu Pin Xuan, Ama Kitchen, and Jin Din Rou all offer better food quality at a lower price. If you’re looking for a beautiful restaurant with excellent service, Black Vinegar is worth visiting. But if your priority is outstanding dim sum, I don’t think the food is worth the premium price. Food: 2/5 | Service: 5/5 | Atmosphere: 5/5 | Overall: 3/5

address: 76 Lê Lai, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: The best Cantonese restaurant in Saigon. Every dish was outstanding, from the succulent roast duck and rich, buttery truffle egg tarts to the perfectly crispy fried sticky rice and the fragrant, naturally sweet mushroom soup. There were seven of us, and we ordered two lunch sets plus half a roast duck, which turned out to be the perfect amount. A special thank you to Chef Leon and the BV team for the warm hospitality and friendly, attentive service. We had a wonderful dining experience.

address: 76 Lê Lai, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Perched on the second floor of the New World Saigon Hotel, Black Vinegar offers a refined yet warmly inviting escape into the world of contemporary Cantonese cuisine. The atmosphere strikes a perfect balance between elegance and comfort—setting the tone for an exceptional dining experience. We were fortunate to experience Chef Leon Lian’s newest creations firsthand, where his creativity truly shines. Each dish arrives as a harmonious blend of flavor, creativity, and visual artistry. The food is deeply flavorful and presented with a beauty that invites admiration before the first bite. What truly elevates the experience is the service. The staff deliver a level of attentiveness that feels both detailed and genuinely personal, anticipating needs with grace and ensuring every moment at the table feels curated rather than routine. Special thanks to Sunny, Chau, Tien, Hai & Huy. We have dined at numerous Michelin-starred restaurants, and Black Vinegar honestly surpassed some of them in flavor. - Abalone Siu Mai With Baby Bok Choy, Served With Abalone Sauce - Japanese Sea Fish with Green Herbs Sauce, served with Cantonese Steamed Rice Rolls - Wagyu Wrapped With Prawn And Mala Sauce - Chicken with Crispy Cantonese Roast Pork Skin, Black Truffle, Char Siu with Salted Egg Yolk

address: 76 Lê Lai, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: One of the best lunches I’ve had in a while. The highlight is definitely the há cảo. The soup comes out at just the right heat, warm and comforting without being too hot, letting the flavors come through clearly. The dumplings are beautifully done, with a soft, thin skin that has just a slight chew, wrapping a juicy, well-seasoned filling. What really stood out is how perfectly they handled temperature throughout the meal. The heat of the soup and the há cảo is spot on, making every bite feel just right. And by the time dessert comes, the gentle coolness is equally well-balanced, refreshing without being too cold. Simple dishes, but executed with real precision. A place I’d happily come back to.

review_text: 5KU Station is one of those places where good food, great vibes, and local culture come together perfectly. Hidden in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City, it’s a lively bar and grill that feels like a modern izakaya with a Vietnamese twist. The open-air setting gives it a casual, social atmosphere — ideal for groups, after-work drinks, or meeting new people. The menu is full of variety, from fresh seafood grilled right at your table to tasty local snacks that pair beautifully with a cold beer. Everything is seasoned perfectly and cooked over charcoal, adding that irresistible smoky flavor. The staff are friendly and quick, even when the place is packed, which it usually is on weekends. Prices are fair for the quality and portion sizes — each dish feels generous. If you want to experience authentic local nightlife with a fun, easygoing crowd and delicious grilled food, 5KU Station is definitely a must-visit in Saigon.

review_text: A small pho restaurant located in an alley, but it's been in business for many years. The broth is light and naturally sweet, not overly strong in flavor. The pho is Southern-style, making it easy to eat and appealing to many people. The meat is tender, the noodles are just right, and the accompanying vegetables are fresh. The space is simple but clean. If you like a delicious, light-flavored, and uncomplicated bowl of pho, this is a place well worth visiting.

address: 16/6 Đường Số 18, Thông Tây Hội, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: I stumbled upon this restaurant by chance; it's only been open for about 10 years, but the food is really good and quite tasty. The broth is slightly sweet, like the Southern style, but that's okay. You can add some fish sauce and herbs to your liking, and it'll be perfectly fine to your preference for a richer flavor. The noodles are thin, like the old-fashioned ones in Saigon, which I really like because I don't like the big, flat ones. They're exactly like the noodles at the famous Nam Huong restaurant on Nguyen Trong Tuyen street. It costs 50k for two dishes and 60k for a mixed dish. I saw they had pork ribs too. I ordered a 50k bowl with cartilage and lean meat, which was delicious. What I liked most was the elderly owner, who spoke softly and calmly. When I asked for more broth, the waitress said, "Please sit down, I'll get it for you," which sounded very humane and hospitable. Because I tend to get up, take my bowl, and ask for a little more broth to make it taste better. There's quite a lot of meat, as you can see in the video, but I've seen many malicious comments criticizing it. From the owner to the waitress and even the security guard, everyone was very friendly and polite. I guess I didn't see any unfair competition or jealous people trying to tarnish the restaurant's reputation. I'm speaking honestly because I've eaten at many restaurants and reviewed many, so I never post negative reviews about places I'm not satisfied with or that aren't good. I only post negative reviews if the restaurant is really unreasonable and disrespectful to customers, because I want to give them a chance to do business. Overall, this restaurant is average to good, very polite and friendly, and definitely worth trying.

review_text: I had a great dining experience here and was impressed by both the quality of the food and the overall atmosphere. The highlight of the meal was definitely the soup. The broth was rich, flavorful, and wonderfully aromatic, with a deep taste that felt carefully prepared. It also had a smooth and slightly creamy texture that made every spoonful comforting and satisfying. The ingredients were equally impressive. The seafood was fresh, high-quality, and cooked perfectly, allowing its natural flavors to shine through. The toppings were generous and complemented the broth very well. I also appreciated the fresh vegetables, which were clean, crisp, and added a nice balance to the meal. The restaurant itself is comfortable and well-equipped. The air-conditioned dining area is cool and pleasant, making it a great place to enjoy a meal, especially on hot days. There is also plenty of parking space available, which makes visiting the restaurant convenient and hassle-free. Considering the quality of the ingredients and the generous portions, I believe the prices are very reasonable. A regular bowl costs 90,000 VND, while the special bowl is 100,000 VND. The small difference in price and the excellent quality make both options a great value for money. Another thing worth mentioning is the service. The staff are friendly, attentive, and very efficient. Even when the restaurant is busy, they remain quick, helpful, and welcoming, which adds a lot to the overall dining experience. Overall, this is a fantastic place for anyone who enjoys flavorful soup, fresh seafood, and quality ingredients. With its rich broth, comfortable air-conditioned environment, convenient parking, fair prices, and excellent service, it is definitely a restaurant I would happily recommend and visit again.

review_text: This is a very small spot where you get to enjoy a very good bạn cũng at a great price! I come to Vietnam to enjoy their cuisine to the fullest. Yes, you can go to a restaurant, order food and get restaurant quality food, but why? Is like going to Italy and, instead of eating at a mommas and pop's place, you go to a fancy restaurant. Get the real food, made from scratch, by a home cook. Yes, from time to time you'll get something you don't like, and that happens everywhere. Now you know not to eat there again and have the choice to share your personal experience too. This is not a fancy place by all means. A small short table, short chairs, probably mismatched bowls so, who cares if the food is delicious!? The woman will prepare it right in front of your eyes! This district of famous for its great street for vendors. Enjoy the food and the whole experience! Isn't that one of the reasons you came to visit Vietnam?

review_text: This is an exceptionally clean local Pho restaurant in District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, where even those sensitive to hygiene can dine with peace of mind! The deep, clear broth is excellent and completely free of artificial flavors. The beef is incredibly tender with no gamey smell, and the pho made with premium, specially-bred chicken is perfectly chewy and moist, not dry at all. They pay great attention to cleanliness, keeping side vegetables in airtight containers and providing individually wrapped cutlery. The dining area, restrooms, and parking lot are all spacious and comfortable. I highly recommend this place to friends and travelers visiting Ho Chi Minh City! (Cash or bank transfer only)

review_text: If you find yourself in District 3, Phở Nhơn is a must-visit. It’s tucked away from the main tourist crowds, offering a much more authentic and relaxed experience. The Experience The restaurant is spotlessly clean, comfortable, and beautifully decorated. It feels like a premium dining spot but at very affordable, local prices. The food is incredibly fresh and flavorful—the broth is a standout—and they have a great selection of fresh drinks to pair with your meal. The Perfect Ending One of the best parts about this location is the neighborhood. After dinner, it is a lovely, easy walk over to Chùa Pháp Hoa (Phap Hoa Temple). Seeing the temple lit up with lanterns right on the canal is the perfect way to end the night. Verdict: Fresh food, great decor, and a beautiful local atmosphere. Highly recommend for a peaceful, delicious night out in Saigon.

review_text: I read reviews before coming here to give it a try and I was disappointed.... it tasted very average and the beef brisket is very tough and chewy, very different from the videos I saw online! the restaurant is also very empty when we arrived, staff not attentive, all doing their own things.

address: 303-305 Võ Văn Tần, Bàn Cờ, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Wowwoowow ok ok, didn't have high expectations coming in but was I wrong. The best pho broth I've ever had. No need to add anything else the taste alone was outstanding and so flavourful. Service was good and the giant plate of greens was awesome too. I will be back for sure!!

address: 303-305 Võ Văn Tần, Bàn Cờ, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: I have had the pleasure of visiting many establishments across Australia, but the service I received at this Vietnamese restaurant was truly exemplary. While I regularly enjoy Pho, this was my first experience authenticating the dish in such a refined setting. The hospitality strikes that perfect balance of professional excellence and genuine warmth, making the entire visit feel special. The quality of the Pho is exceptional—rich, aromatic, and prepared with a level of care that is "spot on." The ingredients are remarkably fresh, with generous portions of both tender meat and crisp vegetables that provide a beautifully balanced and satisfying meal. It is rare to find such high-quality traditional flavours presented with such a modern and professional touch. Logistically, the venue is impeccably maintained, spotlessly clean, and thoughtfully organized, creating a sophisticated yet comfortable environment. I cannot recommend this place highly enough for anyone seeking a premium dining experience delivered with true professionalism. It is a credit to the local community, and I look forward to my next visit.

restaurant_name: Phở SOL - Q4 (Phở & Các Món Ngon Từ Phở)
address: 45 Đ. Nguyễn Trường Tộ, Xóm Chiếu, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: I recently visited this place and noticed that many locals were eating there, which is always a good sign when trying a restaurant in a new city. It immediately gave me confidence that the food would be authentic and worth trying. The restaurant itself was clean, well maintained, and had a comfortable atmosphere. Another thing I appreciated was that the staff could speak English, which made ordering much easier and stress-free. When you’re traveling, that small thing can actually make a big difference. I ordered the Pho Tai Lan, and it turned out to be really good. The broth was flavorful and rich, and the overall taste reminded me of the pho I had in Hanoi. For a moment it almost felt like I was back there again. The portion was satisfying, and everything tasted fresh. Overall, it was a very pleasant experience. Good food, friendly staff, and a nice environment make it a place I would happily visit again. If you’re looking for a solid spot to enjoy Vietnamese pho, this place is definitely worth checking out. I would absolutely recommend it to my friends, and I’m sure I’ll come back again the next time I’m in the area.

restaurant_name: Phở SOL - Q4 (Phở & Các Món Ngon Từ Phở)
address: 45 Đ. Nguyễn Trường Tộ, Xóm Chiếu, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Best northern-style pho in Saigon? This place kinda snatched that title for me—pricey? Yeah. Touristy? For sure. Worth it? Absolutely. Broth’s def on the salty side, but the beef? Tender and juicy. The brisket? Dreamy with that perfect lean-to-fat ratio. And the crispy fried pho? Crunchy, chewy, fun—pls try it. But let’s talk quẩy—golden, crunchy, everything you want from a dough stick. The other sides and desserts? Meh. Just focus on the pho + quẩy combo and you’re good.

review_text: Came here around 11PM and was honestly blown away. This has got to be the best phở I’ve ever had in Vietnam—and that’s saying a lot because I’ve been coming here at least once a year for the past 25 years. The broth was so clean, rich, and full of flavor… you can really taste the quality. Definitely a must-try. And trust me—order an extra bowl of meat on the side… you won’t regret it. 😮‍🔥🍜 Tip: They don’t use hoisin sauce here—and honestly, it’s not even needed.

DON’t order the donuts, unless you like stale crackers that don’t soak up the broth.. ever. 5 stars for the 10 year old boss kid running the show! You don’t come here for the ambiance, it’s a hole in the wall and it should be rated as such.

review_text: I recently stopped by this pho spot, and honestly, the food was just okay. I ordered a bowl of phở bò kho, and while it wasn't bad by any means, it was a little too bland for my taste. Even with the condiments available on the table, I felt it needed more salt and seasonings in the broth itself to bring out the flavors. As for the price, it was pretty much what you'd expect – 55k VND is a typical price for a bowl of phở or noodles in the area. Nothing surprising there. Overall, if you're looking for a quick and simple bowl of phở without too much fuss, this place might work for you. But if you prefer a more robust and well-seasoned broth from the get-go, you might find yourself doing a bit of extra doctoring with the condiments!

review_text: I only came to Pho Trang as my usual Pho restaurant had already closed for the day. The first thing that strikes you about Pho Trang is how clean and organised the restaurant is. You can feel immediately that if they take cleanliness and food hygiene seriously, then the food is also going to be taken seriously. I ordered pho bap gau, and it didn't disappoint. Beautiful clean, fragrant nuoc pho, it's delicate taste brought me back to my dream pho in Hanoi. The price is getting up there for Pho but you can't discount the cleanliness and service of the restaurant, so I feel happy to pay the price. If you're travelling in the Cao Thang area pop in have a delicious bowl of goodness in a clean, spacious and welcoming restaurant, there's even a coffee Roaster above that serves delicious coffee as well. What a perfect start to the morning!

address: 428 Võ Văn Tần, Bàn Cờ, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Phở Trang is seriously impressive. I absolutely loved the broth — rich, clean, and full of depth without being overly heavy. The meat quality is excellent, especially the shoulder clod (lõi vai rùa) — super tender and flavorful. You can really tell they care about sourcing and preparation. Their homemade black hoisin sauce is something special too — thicker, richer, and way more flavorful than the usual bottled version. And don’t skip the bò kho. It’s insanely good. Super tender beef, deeply aromatic, and packed with flavor. Definitely a must-try.

address: 14/5Bis Đ. Kỳ Đồng, Nhiêu Lộc, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: I say, this was the truly local place we went to. You sit in, after going through a small alley, and you feel like you are in a foodcourt. The most refreshing is that there was ALMOST NO foreigners. The waiters had to guess whether we would be comfortable with the Chinese or the English menu (the latter of course). Simply: 1. Big or small portion. 2. What type of chicken part 3. What type of noodles. Menu is a bit complicated but basically it’s that. For me the small portion was enough, we came at 10 am and it seems like this was the locals breakfast. The condiment salad came for free. I suggest to order also the chicken salad which is very tasty. There was only one waiter who spoke English and be patient with him as he has a local pronunciation. Very recommended

review_text: Loved about the big portion, tender chicken slices and lovely broth of the Chicken Pho. Quality and quantity were excellent. 👍🏻 Shredded Chicken Salad was fresh with mountain of vegetables, herbs and chicken meat. It didn’t have much dressing so it would be quite bland if eaten alone but adding to the noodle was excellent. 🙂

address: 14/5Bis Đ. Kỳ Đồng, Nhiêu Lộc, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: My first meal in Ho Chi Minh City! 🇻🇳🍜 The broth is simmered with chicken for hours, giving it a rich chicken flavour while still tasting light and naturally sweet. Even the sliced chicken breast was cooked perfectly—super juicy and not dry at all. I came here wondering if it would taste similar to our Malaysian chicken shredded kuey teow soup. I left with a happy stomach and each has its own unique charm. ❤️

address: 14/5Bis Đ. Kỳ Đồng, Nhiêu Lộc, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam

Food taste ok, nothing wow or bad, but the soup has a lot of fat. I expected the clear broth for this traditional dish. The salad dish has lots of wings bones, not much meat. I am not sure this is normal or I was just in unlucky terms. The total cost is USD $7.32, which is not bad, but I had expected more for this price. Maybe need to try more dishes. Food taste ok, it's the place I would go if the group want to eat there, but it's not the place I really seek to go. If in the area, try it, but not driving far for it

review_text: Pho Huong Binh is a great spot for chicken pho in Ho Chi Minh City. Their Pho Ga is made with free-range chicken, which gives the meat a firmer texture and richer flavor compared to regular chicken. The broth is clear, fragrant, and comforting without being overly heavy. The chicken is tender and flavorful, while the fresh herbs and accompanying vegetables complement the bowl well. Service is friendly, and the restaurant offers an authentic local pho experience. If you’re looking for a good bowl of traditional Vietnamese chicken pho made with quality ingredients, Pho Huong Binh is worth a visit.

review_text: The chicken broth was rich, naturally sweet, and full of flavour. 🍜 The rice noodles were cooked perfectly soft and silky without being mushy. I also loved the Vietnamese Sá Xị. It was refreshing and not overly sweet, which made it even more enjoyable. I want to come back for another bowl! ❤️

I chose chicken thigh to have a better chicken texture, but their chicken was soooo chewy and it’s very hard to bite even the chicken skin. I couldn’t proceed eating and switch with my bf and his beef pho was damnn good. Only cash accepted here.

They’re generous with the herbs and bean sprouts, and that saves the dish for me and nudges me closer to a 5. The atmosphere is meh.

review_text: From the tables to the chopsticks and spoons, everything was clean, and the space was airy and comfortable. The pho was really delicious, the broth was clear. I've eaten at many pho restaurants, but the pho here was truly amazing, completely different from any other I've ever had.

address: 199 Phan Huy Ích, An Hội Tây, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: I stayed at a friend's house to go to a concert. While strolling around, I suddenly had a feeling I wanted to stop and eat at this place. As a result, in the two days I was in Go Vap, I ate pho here two days in a row. The restaurant is super delicious; the broth is sweet and refreshing, and incredibly healing. It's not harsh at all. The pickled garlic is also delicious, and the condiment jars are top-notch, neatly arranged, clean, and complete. The owners are also very lovely. Overall, a perfect 10 out of 10. (Remember to order an extra bowl of egg, it's delicious!)

address: 199 Phan Huy Ích, An Hội Tây, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: I've eaten at many pho restaurants around here, but I think this one sells the best corn pho, and the crispy fried dough sticks are a real treat. The dining area is neat and tidy, with containers for vegetables, making it very clean. I'll definitely be a frequent customer.

address: 199 Phan Huy Ích, An Hội Tây, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: The food was delicious, and even though I have a Central Vietnamese palate, I absolutely loved it. The flavors were well-balanced, rich but not overpowering, and the service was excellent. I added a little more soy sauce and chili. Dipping the crispy fried dough sticks in it, along with a bowl of egg, was the best part.

address: 199 Phan Huy Ích, An Hội Tây, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Wait, it was pinned on Google Maps before, with lots of reviews, someone maliciously deleted it.

address: 76f Phạm Viết Chánh, phường, Thạnh Mỹ Tây, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: It's Pho noodle shop. I think they run business for a while. I remember when I came to Saigon, this shop was here already. It's been more than 10 years since I visited here first. Then also this was the first visit for thia shop Lol. Anyway the I think I had a large bowl with rare meat. The soup, noodle, hearb, sauce on thr table were quite normal and standard. Unfortunately the meat was so hard, but stew meat was soft, so only rare meat was hard... the size was kinda big, so satisfied. The price is normal also as the location.

address: 76f Phạm Viết Chánh, phường, Thạnh Mỹ Tây, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: One of the worst service you can get in Saigon. Phục vụ rất tệ! The Pho is only okay, but service from waitresses to owners just sucks. Servers carelessly cleaning or fill up condiments in front of guests who were eating. Giving attitude and loud chitchatting all the time. Hidden charges and playing dumb to trick customers. I tend to support small local businesses but places like this just be a bad representation and need to be replaced

address: 76f Phạm Viết Chánh, phường, Thạnh Mỹ Tây, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Food was great (recommend Pho Bap). In my opinion, better pho than the Michelin place up the road…. However just be careful with extra charges such as for the wipes on the table, as we thought they were included👍

address: 76f Phạm Viết Chánh, phường, Thạnh Mỹ Tây, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Compared to the other reviewers, it seems I've had a better experience here. I tried it a couple weeks ago. I tried the regular pho with well done meat, and it was surprisingly good. Surprisingly good (to me) because I don't typically like pho. This time, I had the phở bò kho (pho with poached beef). I personally didn't enjoy it as much as the regular pho, but the quality was the same. I wanted a reg, but they said only large was available (at 5pm, 65K/$2.65). The portion size of the pho is very good for people with bigger appetites. I can't say whether the staff is friendly or not. The guy that took my order the first time seemed nice enough. The woman that took my order this time was more blunt. Since the seating is mostly outdoors (with a covering), it's hot while eating. [Update] Bowl of chicken phở, reg size (45K/$1.85). Although the first phở (with beef) I had here was memorably good... The previous time and this time, I don't think tasted as good either time. [Update 2] Regular bowl of phở with well-done beef (45K) is decent, but I've never been able to taste the same flavor as I did the very first time I came here. We got eye rolled by the waitress when we wanted to pay - maybe it's an unintentional reflex she has trying to recall the price we have to pay? Apparently, she does it to my friend every time he comes here and she's the one that's working... it's 2K ($0.10) for a cup of tea water.

address: 76f Phạm Viết Chánh, phường, Thạnh Mỹ Tây, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: TL;DR: bad service, hidden costs, and angry unfriendly owner. Full story: We ordered the beef shank(40k for small /50k for large) and beef rare(25k/30k). We used two wet napkins. Waitor didn’t ask small or large bowl. So we expected to pay at most 80k(see photo of prices in the menu) + napkin fee. The owner(lady with the cash) with lots of unhappy wrinkles etched into her face said each bowl was 60k and napkins were 2k each. So it came out to be 124k. Even let’s say ingredients cost increased... there is no way the 30k rare beef bowl doubled in price. The owner was just angry and yelling and complaining to other customers in the restaurant. Vehemently shaking her head whenever we pointed at the price indicated on the menu. We don’t understand Vietnamese but she kept complaining to other guests in front of us lol other customers just smiled awkwardly.. Afternoon, we went into the cafe Effoc nearby to grab coffee. Coffee shop staff speaks English very well. Asked the staff if she knew this pho place around the corner. “yes”. Is there any reason the beef noodles price can increase up to 120k? . “no” and was pretty shocked. At the end of day, 60k dong is still $3 usd. Whatevs. She can have a blast lol

address: 140 Bành Văn Trân, Tân Sơn Nhất, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Every time my wife and I come back to visit family, we would stay just across the street. Every morning I would walk over and enjoy a bowl of Pho from this restaurant. Some morning I would have them deliver straight to the house. Hands down the best pho. Way better than what we get in Northern California.

address: 140 Bành Văn Trân, Tân Sơn Nhất, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: arguably one of the best breakfast i ever had in my life! the staff is very gentle and they made me try their best seller! recommended 10/10

address: 140 Bành Văn Trân, Tân Sơn Nhất, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Super delicious Pho around the corner from our Airbnb. Quick service and easy to find. I will be coming back! The staff seem friendly and there are plenty of places to site. Tissues are available on the table. The sitting area also has nice greenery

address: 140 Bành Văn Trân, Tân Sơn Nhất, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Tasty Pho, I had been here many times for over 8 years. I still love it so much ❤❤❤

address: 140 Bành Văn Trân, Tân Sơn Nhất, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: I didnt take picture when I was there but the food was pretty good and authentic northerner style. The Pho here is pretty tasty, the broth and texture are strong and flavorful. The hot sauce should be homemade or so because the flavor is unique. The price for 1 bowl was 60.000 vnđ. The ice tea is good too and it's free. Recommended for breakfast and chilling whether.

address: Trần Quốc Thảo/58 Võ Thị Sáu, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Very friendly and warm treatment. I love two elderly there. Not expensive at all and fantastic. Before of the chili tho. It wasn’t a joke but maybe I am just weak. Good to eat alone as well. I m staying here 3 days and gonna eat everyday 🫶

address: Trần Quốc Thảo/58 Võ Thị Sáu, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Hidden gem in the heart of district 3! Great place for breakfast. Very local, the place is extremely clean. Soup is clear and comforting for morning stomach - note, there is no English menu, so come prepared with what you’d like. We ordered the tái = sliced beef & bò viên = beef balls. Both were great! There’s a little monitor to watch over your bikes if you’re parking outside. Really fast service, owners even turn on the other fan for us. Small place as you can expect, cash only.

address: Trần Quốc Thảo/58 Võ Thị Sáu, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Just 45.000vnd, you can choose 2 different types of beef for pho. Small restaurant, few tables but very clean.

address: Trần Quốc Thảo/58 Võ Thị Sáu, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Small space but convenience, clean. Restaurater is friendly and kind. Very good of CCTV for customer to watching their bike on every table. This is my first time to see that kind of security.

address: Trần Quốc Thảo/58 Võ Thị Sáu, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Authentic tiny local place. Excellent quality of pho. Super clean. Everything is in vietnamese be ready.

restaurant_name: Quán Phở Bắc Hải Số 1 Hà Nội
address: 33 Quốc Hương, An Khánh, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: Dropped by this Pho place for lunch. I would say it's just another average pho place. Nothing special about the broth flavor or the atmosphere. Especially compared to all the good pho in HCMC. If you're nearby, give it a try, otherwise, I would say don't go out of your way.

restaurant_name: Quán Phở Bắc Hải Số 1 Hà Nội

review_text: My first 1 star review. This has to be the worst Pho I have ever had. I don’t think they use any bone broth or very little bones to make the beef broth. It was almost like eating hot water mixed with fish sauce. Because all I smell was fish sauce in my broth. They also skim on the meats. They chopped up the meats in small pieces to give an illusion of lots of meats. I would had paid more to add more meats but the meat was not great neither. Very disappointing.

restaurant_name: Quán Phở Bắc Hải Số 1 Hà Nội
address: 33 Quốc Hương, An Khánh, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: A nice local spot for Vietnamese pho, great value just 40 to 60 K. Considering the price and that it’s in Thao dien this is quite good. I will say there’s nothing that stands out about the flavour of soup or meat but if you are ever craving for pho, this will do the job.

restaurant_name: Quán Phở Bắc Hải Số 1 Hà Nội
address: 33 Quốc Hương, An Khánh, Hồ Chí Minh 700000, Việt Nam
review_text: The best Pho I have ever tasted! I was in Vietnam for 5 days and end up eating here 4times. I tried other pho, but this is the best so far !

When compared to other pho I've had this place's fell short. The borth could've been dramatically improved in terms of flavours and the way they cooked the noodles was really making it mushy.

review_text: The beef noodle soup was delicious, and the table was fully stocked with chili sauce, soy sauce, satay sauce, fresh chilies, etc. The ladies in the restaurant were lovely. The bowl of beef noodle soup was very generous.

address: 116 Nguyễn Thị Thập, Tân Thuận, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: The pan-seared beef phở (Phở Tái Lăn) was incredible—bursting with smoky flavor and perfectly tender. As a chef, I really appreciated the depth of the broth and the extra condiments that added to the overall experience. Exceptional first meal in District 7! 10/10.

address: 116 Nguyễn Thị Thập, Tân Thuận, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Came into Saigon late at night and this was nearby to my hotel. The pho was very flavoursome and tasty. Would definitely return if around the area.

address: 116 Nguyễn Thị Thập, Tân Thuận, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Located in the bustling Nguyễn Thị Thập area, just 20 meters from the Nguyễn Văn Linh intersection, this pho restaurant offers a unique take on pho with a variety of topping options. The standout dish is the spicy pho with mixed toppings, especially the rare beef pho with grilled beef (pho trộn tái lăn). The pho noodles are fresh and tender, paired with a rich black soy sauce dressing made from a secret recipe. Toppings include soft grilled beef, tender brisket, and flavorful beef balls. The soup served with the dry pho is clear and light, with a subtle beef broth flavor, although a bit oily. Overall, the pho is delicious and offers a unique twist. However, the prices are a bit high for the quality offered. A downside was that the restaurant ran out of blanched spring onion stems at 11 AM, which is surprising given the early time. Additionally, the staff could be more friendly and professional when serving or handling payment, as there was an unprofessional moment at a nearby table. Required more attention on the ambience of the shop as well.

review_text: ★5 I visited Phở bò Phú Gia and was really impressed. The beef was fresh and tender, and the pho noodles were perfectly smooth and silky, making every bite satisfying. The broth had a clean, comforting flavor that paired beautifully with the ingredients, and everything tasted well-balanced. Despite the quality, the price was very reasonable, which made the experience even better. If you’re looking for delicious and affordable pho, this is definitely a spot worth visiting.

address: 146E Lý Chính Thắng, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 720000, Việt Nam
review_text: Phu Gia offers an authentic and delicious Hanoi flavor! Their stir-fried beef pho is exceptional and a must-try. Pairing it with their crispy fried dough sticks makes the experience absolutely perfect. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a genuine, flavorful bowl of Northern-style pho!

address: 146E Lý Chính Thắng, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 720000, Việt Nam
review_text: Great pho soups with different variations of meat. The portions are decent, meat is plentiful but the broth can be tasteless sometimes, however, there are plenty of condiments to make the broth to your liking. It is slightly on the pricier side (60-80k a bowl), but the food quality reflects it well. Can recommend the "pho bo tai". Note the place closes from noon until early afternoon.

address: 146E Lý Chính Thắng, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 720000, Việt Nam
review_text: Pho was very good. We'd gone there based on the Feed Phil program on Netflix. The service was very cursory. Looked round to see we didn't get any dough sticks or bamboo shoots compared to everyone else. Asked for a sugarcane drink but was told no despite it saying on the wall and other people appearing to have it. Maybe because we asked for it after the main Pho and they just wanted us out for the next customers. Anyway cheap at 4 Pho for £8 or £2 each! We then visited the lady outside who had her sugarcane store and crushed it in front of us which we bought 4 drinks for £1.80 or 45p each. They were delicious!!

address: 146E Lý Chính Thắng, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh 720000, Việt Nam
review_text: I took an Indonesian group there to eat. I never eat here. But my customer seem has a lot of experience with Pho. They eat a lot of Pho at HCM

address: 210 Lê Thánh Tôn, Street, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: We came here because we wanted to try the restaurant that Bill Clinton once visited. The restaurant was clean, modern, and well-maintained. We ordered the chicken pho and the spring rolls with noodles (I forgot the exact name of the dish). The highlight for us was definitely the spring rolls with noodles — super fresh, flavorful, and very satisfying. My mom especially loved the chicken pho. She said it tasted exactly like the pho she usually gets in America, which made her very happy. Overall, it’s a nice spot to check out, especially if you’re curious about the famous history and want a comfortable place for Vietnamese food.

address: 210 Lê Thánh Tôn, Street, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Spring rolls were so yummy! And the seafood pho had fresh flavours, like nothing I’ve tried before. Check it out if you’re staying locally.

address: 210 Lê Thánh Tôn, Street, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Phở 2000 is a must-visit spot in Ho Chi Minh City for anyone craving authentic Vietnamese pho in a relaxed, local setting. This restaurant is famous not just for its long history but for serving one of the most flavorful bowls of pho you’ll find in the city center. The broth is rich yet delicate, perfectly balanced with fresh herbs, tender beef slices, and smooth rice noodles. The place has a cozy and welcoming vibe — a mix of tourists and locals enjoying comfort food after exploring the Ben Thanh Market nearby. Service is quick and friendly, and the prices are fair for the quality and location. I also loved their iced coffee — the perfect pairing with a hot bowl of pho. It’s easy to see why this spot has stayed popular for so many years. Whether you’re visiting Ho Chi Minh for the first time or just want to enjoy a classic bowl done right, Phở 2000 is a timeless local favorite that never disappoints.

address: 210 Lê Thánh Tôn, Street, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: I was staying in the area and decided to drop in after hearing about the history of the restaurant. The beef pho was delicious, very light and refreshing with plenty of meat and noodles. The vegetarian spring rolls were also very fresh and tasty. I would wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to anyone in the area!

address: 210 Lê Thánh Tôn, Street, Bến Thành, Hồ Chí Minh 70000, Việt Nam
review_text: Got to know this restaurant from Best Ever food review show from YouTube. Rather disappointing. The lobster seafood pho is not on the menu. The normal seafood pho tastes similer to light tom yom broth, still full flavour, but compare to the spring roll, it’s much more satisfying than the pho.

address: 69 Trương Quốc Dung, Phú Nhuận, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: My first bowl of pho on this trip and it didn’t disappoint. The dac biet came with a lot of toppings and the broth was fragrant and piping hot. I had to pause to stop sweating as I ate 🥲 very nice staff especially the security at the bottom who went out of his way to help me look for my AirPod bud. It’s upstairs so not ADA accessible. Packed on a regular weekday morning. Might be closed on Buddhist holidays (a lot of restaurants in the area will be)

address: 69 Trương Quốc Dung, Phú Nhuận, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: What a place! Off the main strip this place makes awesome Pho. Servings are massive compared to standard Viet - more like Western portions. Place is up a set of stairs and the broth is light and magical. Very local so don’t expect nice decor be even a fork! Chopsticks only.

address: 69 Trương Quốc Dung, Phú Nhuận, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: If you’re looking for authentic southern-style pho in the city, Pho 69 is the place to go. The broth is deeply flavorful with that perfect southern sweetness, loaded with fresh herbs, plenty of bean sprouts, Thai basil, and lime wedges on the side. It’s hidden on the 2nd floor, it has that cozy, unpretentious vibe that makes every visit feel special. The staff are efficient, the portions are huge, and best of all is that the price is right. You get top-quality pho without breaking the bank. I’m already craving my next bowl. Pho 69 is a solid 5 stars every time! Highly recommend.

review_text: This is the best spot if you want to eat soup pho for more reviews check out my YouTube channel Hollywood's journey

address: 69 Trương Quốc Dung, Phú Nhuận, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Best "Southern style" Pho restaurant in town. Often way too crowded, especially during weekend. My favorite combination is a bowl of brisket and tendon coupled with a small bowl of "nước tiết" (blood cloud, as I call it).

address: 281 Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Very nice owner. Good phở. The marrow (tuỷ bò) and beef tendon (gân bò) are something that you can hardly find elsewhere.

address: 281 Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: _The pho is delicious, the broth is rich and fragrant, the meat is sliced large and thick, 60k for a large bowl (brisket and flank) _The restaurant is clean and tidy

address: 281 Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: The pho is delicious, the broth is clear and flavorful, the prices are reasonable, the staff are enthusiastic, and the restaurant is clean. I've eaten here many times already, it's my favorite pho restaurant ❤️❤️❤️

address: 281 Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: The pho here has a flavorful broth and authentic Southern-style noodles. A full bowl costs 50k and is very generous. I especially like the beef brisket and meatballs. The service is friendly and quick. I will be back soon.

address: 281 Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, Xuân Hòa, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Located in a corner alley, this pho restaurant serves thin noodles. The seasoning was quite good for me, but a little too salty for my wife. However, the toppings were excellent: the tendon was crunchy and fun to chew, the meatballs were flavorful, and the rare beef was incredibly tender without any fishy smell. The staff were very friendly, and served the food quickly and efficiently. I highly recommend this restaurant! 🥰

address: 50 Đ. Quách Đình Bảo, Phú Thạnh, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam

address: 50 Đ. Quách Đình Bảo, Phú Thạnh, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Wow! Pho Tau Bay Tan Phu... True to its name "Tau Bay" (meaning "Airplane"), even big-eaters will find a bowl of mixed pho incredibly satisfying and filling! (55k for a mixed bowl: lots of toppings, including rare beef, brisket, tendon, beef meatballs, and fresh, delicious meat!). A regular bowl is 45k, just right for women, and also has plenty of meat. The pho noodles are soft and perfectly seasoned. The seasoning is light and subtle, with a hint of Saigon-style sweetness. The restaurant is small, clean, and located between two adjacent shops, so there's plenty of seating. The owner and staff are friendly and enthusiastic. Motorbikes can be parked in front of the restaurant. Opening hours: morning to 12 noon.

address: 50 Đ. Quách Đình Bảo, Phú Thạnh, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: The pho was delicious, with plenty of meat. The cooking style wasn't overly strong in spices, but it was incredibly addictive. The owner was lovely. The restaurant is a bit small; it would be perfect if it were a little more spacious. Wishing the restaurant continued success!

address: 50 Đ. Quách Đình Bảo, Phú Thạnh, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: My husband and I stopped by to try it this morning. It was delicious. The last time we ate at a restaurant nearby, their food was too salty 🥸

address: 50 Đ. Quách Đình Bảo, Phú Thạnh, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: The food was average, according to my own taste. The broth was mild and light, not as rich as Southern-style pho, and not as salty as Nam Dinh pho. The scallions were chopped like the authentic "pho tau bay" (airplane pho) on Ly Thai To Street, District 10, but the taste wasn't as good. I asked a neighbor there, they said. The service was quick, friendly, and there was someone to watch the motorbikes. The price was 43k VND per bowl, suitable for students.

review_text: No matter where I live, I always look for a good pho restaurant near my house because I love eating pho all day long, morning, noon, and night. This is my favorite pho restaurant near my house; I've been eating here since I moved to the Tan Binh/Tan Phu area, almost 4 years ago. The Northern-style pho broth isn't too greasy, but it's rich, refined, and perfectly seasoned. The brisket and flank here are delicious, crispy, and sliced into bite-sized pieces. Because they've been around for so long, they've adjusted the recipe slightly to the Southern style, so they include bean sprouts and black bean sauce. The restaurant is open from morning to night, so whenever I crave pho, I can stop by. Almost every weekend in Saigon, I eat rare beef brisket and flank pho here.

restaurant_name: Quán Phở Bát Đàn Hà Nội
address: 268 Đ. Nguyễn Thái Bình, Bảy Hiền, Hồ Chí Minh, Việt Nam
review_text: Authentic Northern-style Pho in the Heart of Saigon! I stumbled upon Pho Bat Dan on Nguyen Thai Binh Street and was truly impressed from the first visit. The broth was clear, subtly sweet, and perfectly captures the authentic Hanoi pho flavor – not overly sweet like some other places. The beef was tender and fresh, especially the rare beef, which was incredibly flavorful. The noodles were soft, not mushy or broken. The restaurant was clean, airy, and had comfortable seating, even though it was quite crowded in the mornings. The service was quick, enthusiastic, and friendly. A big plus is that the restaurant provides plenty of garlic vinegar, fried dough sticks, and fresh vegetables as accompaniments, which were very tasty. The prices were also reasonable considering the quality and ambiance. If you're looking for an authentic Northern-style pho in Saigon, you should definitely try this place. I'm sure I'll be back many more times!

review_text: Delicious! review_text: Man, I totally misjudged Ho Chi Minh City’s bún riêu. While Hanoi’s version is still the GOAT in my book, “Bún Riêu Cô Thủy” here in Saigon is a straight-up masterpiece. For just 50k VND, the bowl is absolutely loaded—pork trotters, congealed blood, crab paste, pork sausage, and tons of snails. The broth has this rich, thick consistency that reminds me of bánh canh, and it’s delicious. The only downside is the lack of AC, so it gets pretty hot, but that’s just the authentic Saigon alleyway vibe for you!

Just note there is no a/c and it is quite stuffy inside. Also, like many local places, not the cleanest. Just forget about it and enjoy the bowl.

They served the soup and its condiments on a separate plate, which made it easy to measure how many additional elements were to your liking. I would also recommend drinking their cane juice. It was delicious, especially in the middle of a hot, humid day.

review_text: Canh Bun Can [Saigon] The restaurant is located in a small alley (next to the railway tracks) on Le Van Sy Street, Phu Nhuan Ward. The space is a bit small; besides the food counter, there are about 3-4 additional tables. Although the space is small, I found it quite clean. The menu and prices are clearly displayed. The tables are fully equipped with spoons, chopsticks, napkins, and condiments such as shrimp paste, tamarind sauce, chili powder, and chili satay. The Canh Bun here is simple, containing only freshwater crab meat, Hue-style pork sausage, and water spinach. It's served with a plate of perfectly cooked blanched water spinach. The broth is light and flavorful, not overly MSG-laden, the crab meat is tender, and the sausage is delicious. The water spinach and water spinach here are especially tender and clean, not tough or fibrous at all, which is a plus. Besides Canh Bun, the restaurant also serves rice noodles, which I found to be good as well. Prices for small, medium, and special bowls are 35,000, 40,000, and 55,000 VND respectively. I usually feel full after eating a medium bowl; those with a bigger appetite can order a special bowl. Motorcycles can be parked inside the house (around 4). The road in front of the restaurant is narrow, so cars cannot enter (if you take a Grab, you'll have to walk into the alley). If you're also a fan of noodle soup, you should definitely try it! Can Noodle Soup Restaurant 🏡 115/47 Le Van Sy Street, Phu Nhuan Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam (formerly Ward 13, Phu Nhuan District) ⏰ Opening hours: 11:00 AM - 7:00 PM (Closed on Sundays)

review_text: If you go to the shop inside the hem (alley), the dining area is a short distance away, and the staff will guide you there. The staff constantly move between the shop and the tables, staying very attentive and being incredibly kind to me as a foreigner. I had heard they serve a "sour cold Pho," but it is actually served at room temperature. Still, having Pho with such a perfectly balanced, tangy, and rich sauce was a first for me—a truly pleasant and fun discovery. Adding the provided chili and fried pork rinds completely changes the character of the noodles, making it even more enjoyable. However, the chili is very spicy, so please add it bit by bit! If the acidity feels too sharp on your tongue, the accompanying soup helps to soothe and balance it out. Even though it was a brand-new experience for me, it was delicious and easy to enjoy. I highly recommend this to anyone looking to try a unique style of Pho. The shop was constantly buzzing with young locals during peak hours, so if you aren't in a hurry, I suggest visiting outside of those times.

review_text: Phở Chua Lạng Sơn - Nguyễn Thiện Thuật This place has been here for awhile and it’s near my house. It serves a dish made from pho noodles from a minority ethnic group in the north. It’s quite interesting to eat a different variation of pho, and I quite like it. If you want to try out a new taste and new dish (and you like sour dishes), I’d recommend this place. The service is quite friendly as well. A bowl is 60.000 VND, not bad. I also got some bánh giò, which is eaten slightly differently than how I would normally eat it, as there is also fish sauce to go along with it, northern style, and there’s a quail egg inside. The taste wasn’t anything special / different; it’s just your typical bánh giò. “Originally from Lang Son, this special dish is the result of the interaction between many cultures of the country.” “Lang Son Sour Pho consists of 2 main parts: dry part and water part. The dry part includes flexible, chewy noodle soup, char siu, cucumber, roasted peanuts, fried sweet potatoes, dried onions, herbs; The water part includes garlic stock, vinegar, and sugar. 2 parts are mixed well for a bar, sweet taste to eat without feeling sick.”

review_text: Ms. Yen's restaurant is very familiar to the people of Binh Thanh District, especially the Thi Nghe area. It's a small eatery, but it's always busy, thanks to its unique "seven days a week" menu: • Monday: Phnom Penh-style noodle soup • Tuesday: Fermented fish noodle soup • Wednesday: Crab noodle soup • Thursday: Braised duck noodles • Friday: Thai noodles • Sunday: Pork offal porridge • Vegetarian days: vegetarian dishes like noodles, stir-fried noodles, or vegetarian broken rice Of these, the two most popular dishes are the fermented fish noodle soup and braised duck noodles. The fermented fish noodle soup has generous toppings, the broth isn't overpoweringly fishy, and it's much more palatable and easier to eat than many other places. The braised duck noodles are also very popular, and sometimes you have to wait for them. The restaurant only has about 3-4 tables, small and compact, but there's always a constant flow of customers. The owners are friendly, kind, and accommodating, making for a comfortable dining experience. Overall, this is a small but great place to eat, the menu changes daily so you never get bored, and it's affordable. Anyone in the Binh Thanh area should definitely try it at least once.

review_text: For me Pho Hanoi hits different than any other Pho. For me Pho Hanoi is dreamy, it's romantic, it encapsulates the feelings and senses that only special food can do. Pho thin does that. Its aroma draws me back those feelings, it's delicious, clear, clean nuoc Pho is so delicate and flavoursome, it's simply outstanding. The restaurant is particularly busy and with good reason. It's fast paced, you order and you pho is on your table before you've had time to look at the historic photos of old Hanoi that adorn the walls. My Pho tai gau is almost perfect in every sense. The only addition was my Trung chan and for me, it goes hand in hand. Travellers, do yourselves a favour, if there's one Pho you try before you leave Saigon, you should make an effort to eat Pho thin.

review_text: Finding a truly soul-warming bowl of noodles in a city as fast-paced as Saigon can feel like a quest, but Phở Bắc 30 in District 4 is one of those rare spots that stops time for a moment. After over 40 years of serving the neighborhood, there is a tangible sense of history and "home" that greets you before you even take your first sip. What struck me most was the broth. It’s deeply savory and clear—true to its Northern roots—carrying the comforting scent of cinnamon and star anise without being overwhelming. I opted for the Phở Bắp Hoa (beef shank), and the meat was incredibly tender, almost melting into the square-cut rice noodles. It felt less like a commercial meal and more like a recipe passed down through generations, which, as it turns out, it actually is. The atmosphere is quintessentially "Saigon." It’s clean and straightforward, with a bustling energy that makes you feel like a local even if it’s your first visit. I loved the little touches: the fresh herbs, the lime wedges, and the option to add quẩy (fried breadsticks) to soak up every last drop of that liquid gold. There’s something deeply satisfying about sitting on a simple stool, steam rising into your face, as the city hums along outside. The only reason I’m holding back that final star is the price-to-portion ratio and the timing. At around 50,000 VND to 65,000 VND per bowl, it’s a bit more expensive than your average street stall, and the portions can feel a little light if you’re coming in with a massive appetite. Also, a pro tip: go early! They often run out of the best cuts (and those delicious breadsticks) by 9:30 AM, so late sleepers might miss the full experience.

review_text: The *bún đậu mắm tôm* here is really enjoyable and quite easy to eat, even for people who are not familiar with strong-flavored dishes. The tofu is fried just right—crispy on the outside while still soft and warm inside, making every bite very satisfying. The *mắm tôm* has a strong aroma at first, but once you mix it with lime, sugar, and chili, the flavor becomes much more balanced and tasty. It turns rich, slightly salty, a bit sweet, and really brings the whole dish together. The set also comes with a good variety of sides like pork, fresh herbs, and noodles, so it feels complete and filling. When everything is eaten together, the flavors blend well—light but still full of taste. The restaurant itself is simple and casual, a nice place for a quick and relaxed meal with friends. Overall, it’s a great spot if you want to try authentic *bún đậu mắm tôm* in an easy and approachable way.

review_text: This is my second time eating here in several years. It costs 85k for a regular bowl and 100k for a special one. But the toppings were terrible (2 small shrimp, 1 piece of squid, 2 pieces of roasted pork, and 1 piece of fish; I didn't eat the fish cake). The shrimp and squid seemed to have been left over from yesterday, so they were incredibly mushy. I'm a big fan of the Bun Mam (fermented fish noodle soup) at Co Ba on Phan Huy Ich street, and since this place is near my house, I decided to try it. It was awful; the toppings weren't even half as good as at Co Ba on Phan Huy Ich street, but the price difference was only 5k. I swear, I was upset after eating two bowls of Bun Mam here. I will never come back and will never recommend this place to anyone. A business that charges high prices but lacks integrity deserves to close down.

review_text: Lucky me. I found this restaurant on my very first day in Ho Chi Minh City! I was just looking for a place to have dinner and ended up here. review_text: Without a question, the best vegetarian restaurant in the entirety of Saigon. Get the Goi Nam Tuyet and thank me later. The waitresses are so incredibly nice and caring. review_text: Lovely vegetarian restaurant. Highly recommend for literally everyone because this place is worth the try. Space: big restaurant with 2 floors. Lots of seating choice. The ambience is warm, kind and cosy with the dimmed orange lights (which is spot on for me who doesn't light extra bright white lights). Seatings are comfy. Tables are big and weren't placed literally an arm length from one another. Food: scrumptious food with lots of choices. Well seasoned, well balance, not too oily. The tofu was a but salty but it was supposed to be paired with rice so no complaint. Their signature rice is great, i could feel the herbaceous aftertaste which was my fave part. Stir fried was fresh. Their spring rolls were super super good, gooey yam fillings. Fried wonton could be improved though since it was a little too flat, there was no volume to the shape, texture while the fillings was spot on. Ice tea is free fyi. Price: super affordable. We had a big meals with 5 dishes or so and it costed 210k, which came to our surprise despite the prices were already listed in the menu lol. It just felt like we ate a lot, that's why. Parking: a bit chaotic since you just park wherever at the fron gate and the security guard would handle the rest. Also, the guard was extremely helpful and polite, this man needs a raise! Overall, such a pleasant experience. Defo coming back to try out more.

review_text: I’ve visited this restaurant three times. During my first two visits with friends, I noticed some unpolished details but overlooked them to avoid seeming upset in their company. This review is based on my third visit, which I made alone, giving the restaurant another chance. The food was neither as flavorful nor as valuable as the menu prices suggested, and the service was genuinely disappointing. The waitress who greeted me was pleasant enough and recommended the restaurant’s bestsellers after placing the menu on the wrong side of the table. Since I prefer spicy flavors, so I requested sliced chilies, but the ones served were dry and old, as shown in the attached photo. After finishing my meal, I asked for the bill. The waitress called over a cashier, who approached me shuffling in slippers and handed me the bill without a word. I paid, and she returned with my change in the same manner—still silent, without a “thank you” or even basic courtesy. She made no eye contact, offered no smile, and left an awkward silence accompanied only by the sound of her shuffling slippers.

restaurant_name: Nhà Hàng Chay Bồ Đề Tịnh Tâm Quận 2

review_text: Ordered the fried rice and garlic tofu. Asked for a pure vegan version, the rice came without any sauce mixed in, did the chef run out of soy sauce? Very lacking of any flavour. The garlic tofu tasted buttery, although I specifically mentioned no dairy. For the price, the food was very underwhelming, I didn't even eat half of it. The entire menu seems to have relatively high prices, especially the drinks. Maybe this is why the restaurant is empty.. Nice cooled AC room, friendly and helpful waitresses, nice design, perhaps some of the other dishes are nicer but I'm not willing to come back again. Edited 19/7 For giving a generic response to me and other reviews that have made comments of the same nature regarding the taste, quality of ingredients and the menu being overpriced.. if you want to answer the review questions, just do it genuinely. Writing a copy and pasted generic message shows insincerity and a lack of real care. I actually brought these issues up with the staff before paying and a good restaurant would have removed the meals from the bill and spoke to management, all I got was a sorry. Obviously this place doesn't care about their customers or their reputation How can this be fixed? There was no refund offered.
